Wall Street bets big on India as IPO boom, private equity and retail investing reshape markets

Blackstone expects its India assets to double to $100 billion in coming years. That’s a sign of the growing sophistication of the financial markets within this $4 trillion economy.

Preeti Singh ,  Ranjani Raghavan ,  Saikat Das  and  Siddhi Nayak

12 October, 2026 08:34 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Blackstone Group COO Jonathan D. Gray stares into the distance. | Photographer: Jose Sarmento Matos/Bloomberg

Follow Us :

Text Size:
A-
A+

-->

Across India’s small towns and bustling cities, retail investors have been snapping up shares of newly listed companies. It’s a boom that Blackstone Inc.’s President Jon Gray celebrates thousands of miles away in his Park Avenue office.

“For us, outside of the United States, India is the most liquid market — the easiest place to get an IPO done in the world this year,’’ Gray said in an interview. India already saw one of its biggest ever initial public offerings in recent weeks and a listing with a market value of more than $100 billion is possible from billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s empire, making the country one of the world’s busiest IPO markets.

Gray and other financial heavyweights acknowledge challenges like rising inflation and the falling rupee. Yet, between its private equity and real estate businesses, Blackstone has listed a string of companies over the past decade in India and revenue growth has been high, Gray said. The firm expects assets under management in the South Asian country to double to $100 billion in the coming years.

Show Full Article

That’s a sign of the growing sophistication of the financial markets within this $4 trillion economy as it opens up further to foreign money. It’s also a dramatic turnaround from just a few years ago when private equity investors had limited options to exit investments in India, let alone at substantial profits. Now private equity, private credit and sovereign wealth funds are committing ever deeper pools of capital, while market makers like Citadel Securities LLC and hedge funds like Millennium Management LLC have built a presence there. Other parts of the financial industry are also changing swiftly.

India’s markets remain a fraction of China’s by size. High corporate taxes and the rupee’s decline leave foreign firms smaller profits to repatriate into dollars. On the political front, a youth protest movement is creating new pressures for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government.

Wall Street bosses are still looking at the economy’s long-term prospects. Many are betting on a series of measures taken by the Modi administration to jumpstart a vast digital payments ecosystem. Millions of Indians are now putting their savings into financial markets for the first time. As new developments reshape Indian finance, here are some of the biggest changes and challenges emerging:

Banking Boom
In recent months, a string of Wall Street bosses have landed in India to court businesses and the government. Citigroup Inc.’s Jane Fraser had a meeting with Modi. JPMorgan Chase & Co.’s Jamie Dimon met the country’s finance minister. Both firms are working on the IPO of Ambani’s digital services giant Jio Platforms. That company is expected to go public later this year at a valuation that could make it India’s largest ever, Bloomberg News has reported.

Banks have been bolstering teams in investment banking and capital markets. Goldman Sachs Group Inc. has injected at least $500 million into its India banking franchise in recent years, Bloomberg News has reported. It’s also one of the banks on the Jio IPO.

“Rapid financialization of household savings is creating a durable pool of domestic capital to support private-sector investment,” said Sonjoy Chatterjee, chairman and chief executive officer of Goldman Sachs India.

The average fee paid to bankers in India has risen to 1.86% of an IPO’s value, according to capital-markets data provider LSEG. That’s higher than roughly 1.5% in Hong Kong.

The firms are all vying for a larger slice of the pie in what’s become one of the world’s most competitive investment banking markets. The Wall Street banks are competing against each other as well as Japanese ones and local firms like Kotak Mahindra Bank Ltd. and Axis Bank Ltd., who command deep client relationships and pricing power.

Meanwhile, global banks are seeing other opportunities. Citi’s India CEO K. Balasubramanian said in an interview that the bank sees added opportunities to do business with local and foreign corporations as India enters into more trade deals with countries including the UK. The India arm of Japan’s Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group Inc. plans to expand its rupee-bond business as companies diversify funding, according to a spokesperson. It has managed about 57 billion rupees ($600 million) of local bonds since the inception of its business in September 2025 and aims to significantly enhance its share over the next two to three years. The firm is also expanding in India’s IPO market.

Private Equity Money
Until the 1990s, India was almost completely closed to foreign capital, and few private equity funds were involved in major deals. As the economy has opened up, PE firms have invested tens of billions of dollars and deal sizes have been increasing.

Brookfield Asset Management Ltd.’s CEO Connor Teskey says that over the next five years the firm’s investment in India will be more than $100 billion from about $30 billion in 2025. It’s a bet on “India’s immense scale, strong economic growth, respect for capital and growing demand for infrastructure,” he said.

Firms like Brookfield and Blackstone are also betting on the country’s real estate markets. Office space has seen a boom as local and foreign companies scramble for room in swanky new towers in cities like Mumbai and New Delhi.

“The one challenge obviously has been higher inflation rates and currency depreciation,” Gray said. Despite that Blackstone has had very good success in areas like its logistics portfolio because “there’s so much underlying demand that you can make up for the fact that the currency’s been going down,” he said.

Global Capability Centers
The basic back-office centers that began in the 1990s have evolved into mission-critical cogs of global finance. India had more than 1,800 Global Capability Centers in 2025 and that is projected to exceed 2,400 by 2030, according to a Dun & Bradstreet report.

While low-end jobs have been shifting to places like the Philippines, the sprawling Indian campuses house armies of quants, risk analysts, investment and tech staff.

GCCs are estimated to have generated around $100 billion in revenue last fiscal year. They have grown so much that some Wall Street giants have more employees in India than anywhere else outside the US. JPMorgan alone has around 60,000 people working at its India GCCs.

Minting Millionaires
Only a small percentage of people in this nation of nearly 1.5 billion people are presently invested in markets, despite recent improvements. Indians save $500 billion annually in financial assets and almost 50% of that is still in cash and deposits, according to analysts at Macquarie.

More of their money may now flow overseas. In recent weeks, India’s market regulator has said it will allow a $463 billion segment of its portfolio management industry catering to wealthy individuals to invest in overseas securities and short equity options.

India’s population of ultra-high-net-worth individuals is forecast to rise from about 19,000 in 2026 to roughly 25,000 by 2031, underscoring its growing role in the global wealth landscape, according to a Knight Frank report. That’s enabled established international private banks like Standard Chartered Plc and HSBC Holdings Plc to build sizeable franchises.

For more, read: Young, Rich, Family Office. Indian Heirs Worry Their Elders

Still, the wealth boom has brought a new set of problems for Modi. As one section of Indian society has grown richer, inequities have deepened and sparked social upheaval. Youth discontent burst into public view this year through the Cockroach Janta Party, a movement that began as satire after a Supreme Court judge compared some unemployed young people to cockroaches. As young people took to the streets  this weekend, the authorities imposed unprecedented restrictions in New Delhi, deploying thousands of police and asking telecom operators to suspend internet services near protest areas. Restrictions across dozens of major roads and intersections were in place in the capital on Monday.

Mixed Markets
While longer term investments have poured in, India’s markets have taken a hit this year as the oil importing country’s currency has slumped and inflation has risen with higher crude prices. Foreign portfolio institutions have pulled out about $30 billion from domestic stocks so far this year in pursuit of artificial intelligence opportunities elsewhere.

While India is among the worst-performing equity markets in 2026, its capital markets have deepened and matured rapidly since the pandemic, underpinned partly by sticky domestic flows, the IPO boom and wide-ranging investment opportunities.

Growing liquidity and institutional participation continue to make the country an important destination in global portfolios. High frequency trading desks run by firms like Optiver Holding BV are going head-to-head with newly minted Indian trading joints and are fueling a fight for top talent. At some high frequency firms, interns have begun to command $31,000 in monthly pay in India.

Regulatory Challenges
New dilemmas are emerging for India’s regulators as its markets become more liquid. Indian retail traders lost more than $9 billion trading equity futures and options in the year ended March.

That’s pushed India’s regulators to clamp down on a boom in the options and futures market, one of the most lucrative areas for foreign trading desks.

The regulator recently accused a small Mauritius-based JPMorgan unit of executing manipulative stock trades in India. The offshore unit’s trading ban has since been lifted. Last year, in one of its most dramatic actions on a foreign firm, SEBI accused Jane Street of market manipulation, an allegation that the US financial giant has denied. The firm has pressed ahead with its case in a high-profile appeal against India’s securities regulator.

GIFT City Rises
A new free market oasis called GIFT City is seeing a boom. Gujarat International Finance Tec-City is part of Modi’s push to develop a hub in India that can compete with major international cities. Foreign banks are seeing assets surge in this alternative low-tax center on India’s west coast. There, they are helping set up treasury operations for corporations, offering financing for international businesses and helping foreign clients trade. HSBC has built a $23 billion balance sheet in GIFT city in under six years, according to people familiar with the matter. Citi’s assets there are likely to reach $3 billion by the end of 2026 from about $350 million last December, its India CEO K. Balasubramanian said.

The hub is “central to the internationalization of India’s economy and to building a global financial hub onshore,” he said. “That makes it a big focus for Citi.”

Saudi Arabia faces new missile and drone fire after major attacks on airports

Saudi Arabia has announced that Riyadh airport will remain shut for now. 

The Kingdom Tower in downtown Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on Oct 12, 2026. (File photo: Reuters)

RIYADH: Saudi Arabia said it was facing a new barrage of incoming fire on Monday (Oct 12) and that Riyadh airport would remain shut for now, days after Saturday's deadly missile strike on a departure terminal that was claimed by Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis. 
Incoming drones and missiles were reported by the Saudi-led coalition backing government forces in Yemen, though there was no immediate news of whether they were intercepted. 
The Houthis have been attacking Saudi airports and oil facilities since last week as part of a rapidly escalating conflict that has spilt over from the wider regional conflagration between the United States and Iran.
Those attacks have shut down parts of Saudi airspace, suspending operations at Riyadh airport, and largely emptying the skies over the capital even as the city hosts a major energy conference.

Saudi Arabia now faces a nightmare predicament, having re-entered Yemen's civil war to push the Houthis from the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait oil route and stop the group making further gains after its sudden advances in September. 
With the Yemeni forces Riyadh supports having made some gains against the Houthis around Bab el-Mandeb but still on the back foot on other fronts, Yemeni military sources said any pressure on the Houthis could take time to pay off. 
Saudi Arabia's long-time regional rival Iran offered to mediate between its Houthi allies and the kingdom. 
"We have repeatedly expressed our readiness to help facilitate dialogue between the parties," foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said on Monday. 
Meanwhile, despite intensified Saudi airstrikes against the group, including what Yemeni television said were hits on al-Jawf province on Monday, the Houthis show no sign of letting up their own barrage of attacks on Saudi infrastructure. 
The group has repeatedly threatened to target airports and airspace, as well as Saudi oil installations that provide the engine for the kingdom's economy and its ambitious development plans. 

Related:

Saudi Arabia says three killed at airport as Yemen war expands

Malaysia urges citizens to postpone Umrah trips as Indonesia calls for vigilance after deadly Saudi airport attacks

UAE CALLS FOR JOINT GULF ACTION Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz Salman said at Monday's conference that the kingdom would stay focused on bringing in investment as part of its wider economic development goals. 
"The development of our energy system and industrial capability continues," he said. 
Saudi Arabia's neighbour, the United Arab Emirates, on Monday called for a revival of joint Gulf action on security and defence in response to the attacks. 
UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash said the targeting of Saudi Arabia undermined the security of all Gulf states and added that the neglect of collective Gulf security had "emboldened others" to overreach against regional states. 
Saudi Arabia and the UAE had been partners in the Yemen conflict for years, but they backed different forces within the Yemeni military coalition supporting the government and fell out last winter. 
US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that Washington was considering joining Saudi Arabia in strikes on the Houthis, but there has been no sign yet of any US action.

Related:

US fears rapid escalation in Middle East after Houthis attack Riyadh

items.title: UK PM Burnham says Iran's IRGC likely behind RAF Fairford incident
items.author: Michael Holden
items.creator: Michael Holden
items.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Monday that a suspected plot targeting the RAF Fairford air base in Britain was "highly likely" to have been coordinated in Iran, and almost certainly directed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
items.body:
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Monday that a suspected plot targeting the RAF Fairford air base in Britain was "highly likely" to have been coordinated in Iran, and almost certainly directed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
The [USN:L1N45R08W TEXT:"RAF Fairford"] base in southwest England, which had been used by US bombers to carry out strikes on Iran, became the focal point for a major security response after five British men were arrested nearby in the early hours of September 27 on suspected terrorism and explosive offences.
US officials have told Reuters that there had been a suspected plot involving Iran to [USN:L1N45S0OK TEXT:"launch a drone attack"], and last week US President Donald Trump said a threat linked to Iran [USN:L1N45R04X TEXT:"had prompted a decision"] to withdraw the bombers from the base.
"I can confirm our assessment that it is highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran, almost certainly directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard," Burnham told parliament.
Iran has rejected any connection with the Fairford incident.
"Tehran has had no involvement in this matter, and if the British government possesses any documents or evidence to support its claims, it should present them," [USN:S8N44X01J TEXT:"said Iran's Ambassador to Britain"], Seyed Ali Mousavi, according to Iran's state news agency IRNA.
FAIRFORD PLOT DETAILS SKETCHY Details around the suspected plot remain thin. The five detained men were later released without charge on police bail "under stringent conditions", and two other arrested men, including a British-Iranian national, [USN:L8N45U0PF TEXT:"have also been released"].
Detectives have said petrol but no viable explosive had been found in vans seized along with the five men. However, both police and Burnham have pointed towards the involvement of a foreign state.
British interior minister Shabana Mahmood told parliament a known individual, whom she did not name, who was based in Iran was believed to be behind what had happened.
"We will not tolerate these threats on our soil," Burnham said. "We will crack down on Iran's use of criminal networks, using our full range of powers to target them and their funding streams, and we will bring further sanctions to restrict the capacity of Iran and the IRGC to do us harm."
Foreign ministries from almost 30 countries including the US, Canada, France and Germany issued a statement condemning "Iran’s use of violent attacks, including the acts of lethal plotting, arson, sabotage, cyber-attacks, and other hybrid activities against us and our partners".
"The UK has also concluded this event demonstrates the IRGC’s continued willingness to project hostile activity beyond its borders through covert networks and proxy actors," the statement said.
The British authorities have for a number of years accused Iran of being involved in numerous plots and attempted assassinations in Britain using criminal networks and proxies, accusations Tehran has repeatedly denied.
Last year Britain said there had been 20 credible Iranian-backed threats to kill or kidnap individuals based in the UK.
In July, Britain used new powers to ban support for the IRGC and a linked group, Harakat Ashab al-Yamin al-Islamiya (HAYI), which had claimed responsibility for seven attacks earlier this year at locations linked to Jewish and Israeli communities, and Persian-language media.
British foreign minister Ed Miliband said he had summoned the Iranian ambassador while the ministry announced two Iranian nationals [USN:S8N44301J TEXT:"had been sanctioned"].
The two men were Ruhollah Bazghandi, who Britain said was the IRGC's head of counterespionage operations, and Shahram Ali Reza Tamarzadeh Jakki, a facilitator for the already sanctioned Zindashti criminal network which is accused of involvement in several plots against Iranian dissidents.

LONDON, Oct 12 : Players who sign up for LIV Golf next season will not be allowed to become members of the European Tour, DP World Tour Chief Executive Officer Guy Kinnings told the BBC on Monday.
Kinnings said that players must now make a choice.
"We have rules and regulations which are there to protect our tour and which our members must all abide by. Players who are not willing to comply with our rules and regulations should not be seeking to join our tour," he added.
LIV Golf was not immediately available for comment.

Some top players were given conditional releases by the European Tour in the past which allowed them to  compete in both.
Membership of the European Tour is a requirement to play for Europe in the Ryder Cup.
Former world number one Jon Rahm has said he will not be participating in LIV Golf, which is fighting to emerge from Chapter 11 bankruptcy after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew financial support and has secured funding from BC Partners Credit.
LIV has agreed to terminate Sergio Garcia’s contract and Bryson DeChambeau, Cameron Smith, An Byeong-hun, Marc Leishman, Cameron Tringale and Matthew Wolff are seeking release from old deals.
The BBC said it had been told DP World Tour will not accept membership from anyone intending to play in the latest version of LIV. It added that the tour would have grounds to terminate the membership of anyone who did not disclose their intention to play with LIV and then played.

items.title: Nigeria's Dangote refinery extends $1.6 billion IPO to broaden African investor access
items.author: Chijioke Ohuocha, Macdonald Dzirutwe
items.creator: Chijioke Ohuocha, Macdonald Dzirutwe
items.summary: Nigeria's Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals has extended the application period for its initial public offering by two weeks to October 27, citing strong investor interest across Africa and efforts to broaden access to the share sale.
items.body:
Nigeria's Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals has extended the application period for its [USN:L1N456052 TEXT:"initial public offering"] by two weeks to October 27, citing strong investor interest across Africa and efforts to broaden access to the share sale.
The company said on Monday that Nigeria's Securities and Exchange Commission had approved the extension of the offer, which opened on September 14 and had been due to close on October 13.
Reuters earlier reported the extension of what is set to be Africa's largest share sale.
The refinery, owned by Africa's richest person, Aliko Dangote, is seeking to broaden ownership of its 700,000-barrel-per-day complex through an offer aimed at up to 10 million retail investors in Nigeria and elsewhere across the continent.
The company said the extension would support market-access initiatives in other African countries, including expanding distribution channels and facilitating cross-border investment.
It said the additional time would also allow prospective investors to complete account-opening procedures, identity verification checks and other regulatory requirements needed to participate in the offer.
The prospectus showed the share sale was not registered as a public offering outside Nigeria, forcing investors to rely on local regulations or gain access through a limited number of eligible online investment platforms.
The mismatch between Dangote's pan-African ambitions and the uneven take-up beyond Nigeria highlights how fragmented capital markets continue to hinder [USN:L8N45D1AE TEXT:"cross-border investment"] across the continent.
The IPO aims to raise around $1.6 billion — or up to $2.1 billion if an over-allotment option is exercised — from retail investors to help fund the expansion of the Lagos refinery.
The refinery, which began processing crude in early 2024, is central to Nigeria's efforts to reduce fuel imports and become a net exporter of refined petroleum products.
The offering is viewed as a major test of pan-African retail investor appetite for ownership in a large industrial asset.

PARIS, Oct 12 : Hackers forced the temperature of many French supermarket fridges up to 50 degrees Celsius (122°F) overnight, causing fires and food losses at several hundred stores across the country in a major cyberattack.
The Paris prosecutor's office said a "large-scale" attack was "affecting connected refrigerators in several major food retailers across France" and reported damage included "food losses and fires".
Meanwhile, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu instructed France's National Cybersecurity Agency ANSSI to investigate, a person in his office said.
They said France "was coordinating with its European counterparts, as other countries may also be affected," while also investigating whether any other French firms were at risk.

Les Mousquetaires, which owns retailer Intermarche, said around 150 of its stores had been hit, with fridges heated up to 50 degrees Celsius for six hours. It had thrown all the food away to avoid any sanitary risks, a spokesperson said.
And Cooperative U CEO Dominique Schelcher said his supermarket had also been hit by the attack.
"Targeting equipment essential to the preservation of fresh products and to the food supply of the French people is of extreme gravity and is unprecedented," he wrote on X.
Carrefour said 80 of its supermarkets had been hit but that the vast majority of its 6,000 stores had not been affected. 
Several other supermarket chains, including Monoprix, E.Leclerc and Auchan, did not respond to requests for comment.
DUTCH SECURITY ISSUE
Dutch supermarket operator Ahold Delhaize, which operates the Netherlands' largest supermarket chain Albert Heijn and has substantial operations in the United States, said it was also dealing with a "security issue" in its network, and had taken several systems offline to protect them.
A smartphone app for the retailer told clients that due to a "cybersecurity incident" it was unable to deliver groceries.
Online orders represent around 10 per cent of sales for Albert Heijn. Physical stores remained open and Dutch news agency ANP reported that rivals had seen an influx of delivery orders.
It was not clear if there was any link between the French supermarket attack and the problems flagged by Ahold Delhaize. 
Ahold is the fourth-largest grocery retailer in the US, where websites for its Stop & Shop, Giant, Hannaford and Food Lion stores all had notices saying "site temporarily down".
It was unclear if other operations were affected.
The source close to Lecornu said ANSSI had identified a vulnerability in software supplied by Danish company Danfoss.
Danfoss said it was "aware of incidents in France affecting a limited number of refrigeration management systems".
The affected units "were running outdated firmware", Danfoss said, adding that it had "long advised customers to keep supported systems updated with the latest firmware and to migrate legacy systems to current-generation solutions".   

Source: Reuters

items.title: Hackers heat French supermarket fridges, sparking fires and spoiling food
items.author: Leo Marchandon, Gabriel Stargardter
items.creator: Leo Marchandon, Gabriel Stargardter
items.summary: Hackers raised the temperature of refrigerators and freezers at hundreds of French supermarkets to as high as 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) overnight, causing fires and spoiling food.
items.body:
Hackers raised the temperature of refrigerators and freezers at hundreds of French supermarkets to as high as 50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit) overnight, causing fires and spoiling food.
The Paris prosecutor's office said on Monday that a "large-scale" attack was "affecting connected refrigerators in several major food retailers across France", leading to food losses and fires.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has instructed France's National Cybersecurity Agency (ANSSI) to investigate, a person in his office said.
France was coordinating with European counterparts because other countries could also be affected, the person said, adding that authorities were assessing whether other French companies were at risk.
Felix Aime, a senior cyber threat intelligence analyst at Sekoia Threat Detection and Research, said Spain, Portugal, Poland, Germany and Belgium had also been affected.
Carrefour (CARR.PA) said 80 of its supermarkets were hit, while Monoprix, which operates about 490 stores in France, said 5% of its stores were affected.
Les Mousquetaires, owner of retailer Intermarche, said fridges at around 150 of its stores were heated up to 50 C for six hours overnight. A spokesperson said all affected food had been discarded to eliminate health risks.
Paris resident Geert de Clercq witnessed staff at an Intermarche in central Paris throwing cartfuls of defrosted frozen foods into a giant trash container, with molten ice cream sloshing out of broken tubs on the street.
Cooperative U CEO Dominique Schelcher said his supermarket group had also been targeted.
"Targeting equipment essential to the preservation of fresh products and to the food supply of the French people is of extreme gravity and is unprecedented," he wrote on X.
Food retailers E.Leclerc and Auchan did not respond to requests for comment.
There was no immediate estimate of industry-wide losses, but Intermarche CEO Thierry Cotillard told BFM TV the "unprecedented" attack would represent losses amounting to "tens of millions of euros nationwide in a single day."
Christel Delberghe, director general at European retail association Eurocommerce, said, "This incident underlines the importance of resilience across the entire supply chain."
COLD AISLES CONTROLLED OVER INTERNET Supermarket cold aisles are typically run by control panels that manage an entire store's fridges and freezers and can be accessed over the internet, which lets maintenance companies adjust them from anywhere.
The source close to Lecornu said ANSSI had identified a vulnerability in software supplied by Danish company Danfoss.
Danfoss said it was "aware of incidents in France affecting a limited number of refrigeration management systems".
The affected units "were running outdated firmware", Danfoss said, adding that it had "long advised customers to keep supported systems updated with the latest firmware and to migrate legacy systems to current-generation solutions".
On August 9, cybersecurity firm Claroty's Team82 published research detailing vulnerabilities in the Danfoss AK-SM 800A controller. According to the report, software updates issued by Danfoss addressed issues that could have allowed attackers to bypass authentication controls and execute code on compromised devices.
The attacks resemble disruptions reported at about a dozen US military commissaries in late August that led to food losses after fridges were affected.
In a statement, French retail association Fédération du Commerce et de la Distribution called for "full transparency" from Danfoss about the incident. It said supermarkets aimed to protect consumers and return to normal operations as soon as possible. The FCD said some impacted stores were already back up and running.
DUTCH SECURITY ISSUE Dutch retailer Ahold Delhaize (AD.AS) , which operates the Netherlands' largest supermarket chain Albert Heijn and has major operations in the US, said it was dealing with a "security issue" on its network and had taken several systems offline as a precaution.
A message on the retailer's smartphone app said it was unable to deliver groceries because of a "cybersecurity incident".
Online orders account for about 10% of Albert Heijn sales. Physical stores remained open, while Dutch news agency ANP reported that rival retailers had seen a surge in delivery orders.
Ahold Delhaize said there was no reason to see a link between the incidents in France and its supermarkets.
Ahold is the fourth-largest grocery retailer in the US. Websites for its Stop & Shop, Giant, Hannaford and Food Lion chains displayed notices saying "site temporarily down".
It was unclear whether other operations had been affected.

items.title: Hurricane Simon crawls along Mexico's Pacific coast, bringing floods and evacuations
items.author: Alberto Fajardo, Daniel Becerril
items.creator: Alberto Fajardo, Daniel Becerril
items.summary: Hurricane Simon crept northwest just off Mexico's Pacific coast on Monday, lashing western states with dangerous winds, heavy rain and flooding that put riverside communities on alert for possible evacuations.
items.body:
Hurricane Simon crept northwest just off Mexico's Pacific coast on Monday, lashing western states with dangerous winds, heavy rain and flooding that put riverside communities on alert for possible evacuations.
The US National Hurricane Center said Simon was about 55 miles (90 km) west-southwest of Cabo Corrientes in Jalisco state at 8 a.m. (1400 GMT), packing maximum sustained winds of 110 mph (175 kph), making it a Category 2 hurricane.
Simon has weakened since Saturday when it was a Category 4 system.
"Simon is slowly losing wind intensity and could ultimately stall this week and never make a true landfall as an organized storm," said Alex DaSilva, a hurricane expert at private forecaster AccuWeather.
Simon is forecast to make landfall on Thursday in Mexico's Sinaloa state.
"The slower Simon moves, the more rain potential the storm carries, but right now most of that rain is offshore and to the south of the storm's center ultimately sparing the feet of rain we thought this storm could initially bring," said DaSilva.
Simon was moving northwest at just 3 mph (6 kph) and was expected to continue along that track before turning northeast and moving inland across west-central Mexico around midweek.
Authorities said that Simon could bring life-threatening flooding and mudslides to parts of the Pacific coast and nearby mountains.
The hurricane is forecast to dump an additional 2 to 4 inches (5 to 10 cm) of rain across coastal areas of southwest and west-central Mexico, with isolated amounts of 6 to 8 inches (15 to 20 cm) in parts of Jalisco and Sinaloa. The National Hurricane Center said isolated storm totals could reach 30 inches (76 cm) in parts of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco.
The head of Mexico's civil protection agency, Laura Velazquez, said one person was reported to have died due to the storm in Guerrero state, home to the popular tourist destination of Acapulco.
In the coastal town of Cihuatlan in southwestern Jalisco, patrols warned residents to prepare for potential evacuation as the Marabasco River rose. Floodwater inundated streets and low-lying areas of the town overnight.
In the port city of Manzanillo in Colima state, residents waded through flooded homes and streets as navy personnel helped remove water.
"Everything got flooded," said resident Maria Elena Vazquez from inside her home, pants rolled up as the water came up to her ankles.
The National Hurricane Center said Simon was expected to produce dangerous storm surge and large destructive waves close to where it approaches the coast. Swells from the hurricane are also forecast to create life-threatening surf and rip current conditions along southwestern and west-central Mexico over the next few days.
Following weeks of storms that have battered Mexico, at least 10 people are missing in the state of Baja California and one minor was killed in the coastal city of Ensenada.

FAST

LONDON, Oct 12 : Britain's AI Security Institute has been given access to the latest advanced AI models and is working with the US government and major developers, including Google, to assess their safety, AI Minister Kanishka Narayan said on Monday.
Britain, which is not home to any major AI developers, is seeking a leading role in efforts to assess and manage the risks posed by increasingly powerful AI systems.
Scrutiny of AI safety has intensified after developers including Anthropic and OpenAI disclosed instances of rogue or undesired behaviour by AI agents. Some industry figures have warned the technology could pose an existential threat to humanity.
Monday's announcement, which did not specify all the models the institute is evaluating, comes after reports last month that the White House has asked OpenAI and Anthropic to withhold new models from British testers pending a US review.

"I can confirm that AI scientists at the AI Security Institute are now conducting rigorous evaluations of the latest generation of models, including Gemini 4 Argon, to identify risks early, to test robust safeguards, to help keep people safe," Narayan said.
Under voluntary agreements with major AI developers, the institute receives access to models before deployment, allowing it to assess their capabilities and risks and contribute to emerging international safety standards.
Microsoft President Brad Smith said in an interview published by the BBC on Monday that Britain was well placed to help lead work on AI safety guidelines.
In a letter published in September, the AISI said Anthropic had made clear that no organisation outside the US had access to its Mythos 5.1 model.
Asked about access to frontier AI systems — something ministers have never confirmed the institute had lost on a wider basis — Narayan said the government had a long-standing relationship with the US built on trust.
"When you're reliant on someone else's technology, you have to be clear-eyed about the permanence of any outcome. But I'm very confident that, as a consequence of the conversations we've had, we will be able to test the latest generation of models," he said.

Source: Reuters

items.title: Frasers increases Burberry stake again as it expands luxury interests
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: British retailer Frasers has further increased its stake in luxury brand Burberry to 7.42%, having already raised its holding at the end of September, as the Mike Ashley-controlled company broadens its interests in the luxury sector.
items.body:
British retailer Frasers has further increased its stake in luxury brand Burberry to 7.42%, having already raised its holding at the end of September, as the Mike Ashley-controlled company broadens its interests in the luxury sector.
The owner of Sports Direct is known for aggressively buying up retailers, and in August [USN:L6N44A0S4 TEXT:"bought"] luxury department store Harvey Nichols out of administration, as well as pursuing a [USN:FWN4530VJ TEXT:"takeover"] of Hugo Boss.
Frasers had on September 30 disclosed a stake of 6.32% in Burberry, up from 4.16% previously. Its stake is held entirely via sold put options with expiries of October 2026, March 2027, and September 2027.
Burberry declined to comment, and Frasers did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the increased stake. Frasers last week set out a luxury strategy, saying it sees opportunities to expand its department store chain Flannels in Europe and Harvey Nichols globally.

items.title: Starbucks says not buying Chipotle, ends takeover speculation
items.author: Anuja Mistry, Neil Kanatt
items.creator: Anuja Mistry, Neil Kanatt
items.summary: Starbucks is not buying Chipotle Mexican Grill , the coffee chain said on Monday, quashing talk of a deal that could have been the largest-ever involving restaurants but was doubted by both investors and analysts.
items.body:
Starbucks (SBUX.O) is not buying Chipotle Mexican Grill (CMG.N) , the coffee chain said on Monday, quashing talk of a deal that could have been the largest-ever involving restaurants but was doubted by both investors and analysts.
"As a matter of policy, we don't comment on rumors and speculation, but we want to be clear we are not buying Chipotle," a Starbucks spokesperson said. Chipotle declined to comment.
The statement follows [USN:L6N45U0YK TEXT:"a report by the Financial Times on October 8"] that Starbucks had worked with advisers in recent months on a potential proposal to acquire Chipotle, citing people familiar with the matter.
Starbucks did not respond to a request for comment on whether they approached advisers for a deal.
Shares of the coffee chain were up 1% in early trading, while Chipotle, whose shares surged on the prospect of a takeover which would have reunited Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol with the burrito chain he led for six years, fell about 4%.
Starbucks also reiterated that its management was "laser focused" on "Back to Starbucks" strategy and had "strong momentum and confidence" in its long-term growth prospects. The company aims to share its fourth-quarter results and fiscal 2027 outlook later this month.
Starbucks shares have gained 7.8% this year, roughly half the gain in the S&P 500 over the period. The chain has been closing [USN:L4N45G0UG TEXT:"dozens"] of underperforming stores as part of a turnaround led by Niccol, who has tried to draw back customers with shorter wait times and simpler menus.
TAKEOVER SPECULATION The report of a potential deal last week prompted the investor community to speculate about a tie-up that would have brought together two of the largest US restaurant brands.
Chances of a deal sent Chipotle shares up more than 7% and Starbucks down about 3%, even as several analysts questioned the strategic rationale as Starbucks was in revival mode under Niccol.
"Rumors like these can prime investment bankers to start fantasizing about all sorts of tie-ups, but they're a tough sell. The tide has been shifting more toward divestitures than acquisitions," From Brian Jacobsen, chief economic strategist at Annex Wealth Management said.
A potential deal would have created a restaurant giant with about $50 billion in annual sales, positioning it to better navigate uncertain demand from inflation-hit consumers, rising operating costs and the squeeze on profits. The burrito chain has a market capitalization is around $40 billion.
NICCOL'S CHALLENGE "Funding a premium takeover price would likely require a mix of debt and equity, which would test leverage and could dilute existing shareholders while Starbucks is still executing its turnaround," Paren Knadjian, Partner at Transaction Advisory Services, EisnerAmper said last week.
Niccol joined Starbucks in 2024 after leading Chipotle through a period of rapid growth and digital expansion.
He was credited with reviving the burrito chain after its food-safety crises and expanding its digital business, helping accelerate sales growth.
Chipotle, meanwhile, has grappled with softer traffic as consumers cut back spending, while higher food and labor costs hurt margins across the restaurant industry. Their shares have nearly halved in value since Niccol's departure.

items.summary: [ドバイ １２日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ドバイ １２日 ロイター] - イラン外務省のバガイ報道官は１２日、ホルムズ海峡の再開に関するイランの提案に対する米国の回答は依然精査中だと述べた。精査が終わり次第、仲介者を通じて米政府に返答するとしている。

バガイ氏は、イランは仲介者を通じてメッセージのやり取りを続けているとも述べたが、詳細には触れなかった。

イラン最高安全保障委員会のレザイ事務局長は、米国の回答は「不十分」だったと述べた。国営メディアが１１日報じた。

サウジアラビアとイエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派の衝突が激しくなっていることについて、バガイ氏は、対話による危機の解決に協力する用意があるというイラン政府の立場を改めて示した。

「イエメン問題は（国連の）ロードマップ（行程表）によってずっと前に解決しているべきだった。われわれは、イエメンとサウジの間で成立するいかなる合意も支持すると表明していた」とし、対話を通じた解決を望むと述べた。

FAST

Oct 12 : Global smartphone shipments fell 20 per cent on-year to their lowest third-quarter level since 2012, as soaring memory chip costs and supply shortages pressured manufacturers and pushed up prices, preliminary estimates from Counterpoint Research showed on Monday.
Rising prices for memory components as AI infrastructure projects corner supplies have driven up production costs and prompted manufacturers to raise retail prices, cut shipments and prioritize profitability over volumes.
"Consumers are holding on to their devices longer than estimated, increasingly considering refurbished devices and prioritizing higher-value devices," said Counterpoint senior analyst Shilpi Jain.
Samsung retained its top position with a 23 per cent market share, helped by demand for its Galaxy Z Fold8 series and stable component supplies for its mid-range devices. Shipments fell 3 per cent from a year earlier during the quarter.

Oct 12 : Global smartphone shipments fell 20 per cent on-year to their lowest third-quarter level since 2012, as soaring memory chip costs and supply shortages pressured manufacturers and pushed up prices, preliminary estimates from Counterpoint Research showed on Monday.
Rising prices for memory components as AI infrastructure projects corner supplies have driven up production costs and prompted manufacturers to raise retail prices, cut shipments and prioritize profitability over volumes.
"Consumers are holding on to their devices longer than estimated, increasingly considering refurbished devices and prioritizing higher-value devices," said Counterpoint senior analyst Shilpi Jain.
Samsung retained its top position with a 23 per cent market share, helped by demand for its Galaxy Z Fold8 series and stable component supplies for its mid-range devices. Shipments fell 3 per cent from a year earlier during the quarter.

items.title: サウジ首都の空港が閉鎖延長、フーシ派攻撃で被害　経済への影響懸念
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Gianluca Lo Nostro　Menna AlaaElDin

［１２日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Gianluca Lo Nostro　Menna AlaaElDin

［１２日　ロイター］ - サウジアラビア当局は１２日、週末にイエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派の攻撃を受けた首都リヤドのキング・ハリド国際空港の運用停止措置を延長した。

サウジ民間航空当局は、空港閉鎖について、「空港施設の安全と運用準備態勢を確保するための手続きを完了させる」ためだと説明した。

同空港の利用者数は、ジッダに次いで国内２番目に多い。一連の攻撃は、サウジ航空業界に混乱をもたらすとともに、航空燃料の高騰に直面している航空会社にさらなる打撃となっている。

航空データ分析会社シリウムによると、同空港では１２００ＧＭＴ（日本時間午後９時）時点で予定されていた全便の８２％が欠航となっている。最終的な数字はさらに高くなる可能性があるという。サウジ国内の全空港での欠航率は４６．４％に達した。

航空機追跡サイト「フライトレーダー２４」のデータによると、航空機は１２日、リヤドを避けて飛行している。ただ、サウジ領空を通過し、西海岸の主要拠点であるジッダに着陸する便は見られた。

混乱を受けて欧州やアジアの航空各社は運航停止を余儀なくされている。欧州航空安全庁（ＥＡＳＡ）は９日。ミサイルや無人機（ドローン）による攻撃を理由に、サウジ領空に関する警告の対象範囲を拡大した。米連邦航空局（ＦＡＡ）は１１日、米国の航空会社に対し、サウジへの飛行や領空通過の際に警戒するよう勧告した。

ルフトハンザ・グループはリヤド便を１０月１６日まで全便欠航とし、エールフランスＫＬＭはリヤド発着便の運航停止措置を今月末まで延長した。

アブダビのエティハド航空もサウジ便の欠航延長を決め、１２日と１３日にリヤド、ジッダ、ダンマンを結ぶ約２０便に影響が出た。

今回の攻撃は、今月リヤドで開催予定の大規模会合にも影を落とす。世界石油会議（ＷＰＣ）の会合は、複数の石油大手トップが参加を取りやめた。

フーシ派との衝突激化により、より広範な経済的影響への懸念が強まっている。サウジの実質国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）は、石油活動の低迷など複数の要因を反映し、２０２６年に３．６％縮小すると予測されている。

What Trump’s Russian diesel deal means for US, surging global prices & Indian refiners

The US has eased sanctions on Russian diesel to address fuel-price pressures, raising questions over its Russia policy and the outlook for Indian refiners.

Udit Bubna

12 October, 2026 06:27 pm IST

Facebook

File photo of Russian President Vladimir Putin with his American counterpart Donald Trump | Reuters

Follow Us :

Text Size:
A-

New Delhi: US President Donald Trump’s decision to bring Russian diesel back into the American market has raised questions about Washington’s sanctions policy against Moscow and its efforts to curb revenues funding the war in Ukraine.

Trump’s decision comes ahead of the November mid-term elections, with diesel prices near record levels. Diesel is essential for trucking, agriculture and heating in the US, making higher fuel costs a concern for households and businesses.

The announcement on Friday came less than a month after Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which provides for tariffs of up to 100 percent on goods from countries that continue to buy Russian oil and gas under specified conditions.

Show Full Article

On 9 October, the US Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) issued General License 135, temporarily authorising specified transactions involving Russian-origin diesel until 7 April 2027, allowing the proposed trade to proceed.

However, analysts are sceptical that the additional volumes will significantly ease global diesel shortages or bring down prices across markets.

Abu Dhabi-based commodity analyst Natalia Katona said the arrangement appeared to be directed at a specific regional market rather than the global diesel shortage. “The US Atlantic coast, particularly New York and the wider Northeast, has a persistent diesel shortfall because it lacks sufficient refining capacity.” .

Regular seaborne imports of around 200,000-300,000 barrels per day help meet that shortfall, Katona said.

“While many in the market argue that these volumes won’t solve the global diesel shortage, Trump is addressing a very specific local problem: diesel prices in the traditionally Democratic Northeast ahead of the elections,” she told ThePrint.

Also Read: India’s now importing pre-conflict levels of Gulf crude; share of Russian oil lowest since April

Sanctions relief versus pressure on Russia
Trump’s move highlights the contrast between the US easing restrictions on its own proposed Russian diesel imports and threatening penalties against other major buyers of Russian energy.

America-based energy strategist and geopolitical analyst Umud Shokri said the arrangement was administratively permitted under the US licence, but actual deliveries would depend on available Russian supplies, export rules, shipping and payment arrangements. He also noted that some US lawmakers had questioned whether the move conflicted with federal law.

Russia’s own restrictions could pose another constraint. Moscow extended its diesel export ban for producers until 31 October, citing the need to stabilise domestic fuel supplies. Meanwhile, Ukrainian drone attacks continue to disrupt Russian refining capacity.

Despite restrictions on diesel exports, Russia continued supplying some foreign markets during the sanctions period through government-to-government arrangements which was exempt from its export ban, Katona said. These shipments included supplies to Mongolia, Kyrgyzstan and other Central Asian countries.

Shokri said there was no indication that Russian refineries returned to peak operating levels. In September, half of Russia’s six largest diesel-producing refineries had significantly reduced or halted output following drone damage, he said.

Under Trump’s supply arrangement, Russia is expected to ship 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately, followed by 500,000 tonnes in November and one million tonnes in December, according to Katona.

These volumes would be equivalent to around 75,000 barrels per day (b/d), 125,000 b/d and 250,000 b/d, respectively, averaged over a month. The December shipment could cover almost all of the US Northeast’s regular diesel import requirement of 200,000-300,000 b/d.

However, high freight rates and a shortage of clean-product tankers could limit the wider impact, as diesel markets have become increasingly regional.

Russia, according to Katona, last supplied diesel to the US in 2022, with arrivals peaking at 210,000 tonnes in December that year. No cargoes have arrived since 2023.

What it means for India’s oil trade
For Indian refiners, the bigger risk lies in changing regional trade flows and potential pressure on export margins rather than direct competition from Russian diesel in the US.

India exported 630,000 barrels per day (b/d) of diesel in September, of which Europe took 280,000 b/d. These shipments had largely been contracted one to two months earlier, Katona said.

The outlook will depend on whether China resumes larger diesel exports and how shipping costs to Europe evolve.

“If China starts flooding the Singapore and Southeast Asian markets, India will have no option other than to re-orient flows towards East Africa and Europe,” Katona said.

China’s planned return to diesel exports has already pushed down refining margins in Singapore to $64-65 per barrel, she added. If shipping costs to Europe remain high, Indian refiners may find it more profitable to sell their diesel in Asian markets instead.

Shokri said a possible recovery in Russian diesel production and exports could increase competition for Indian fuel, particularly in Europe, where shipments grew in September. The greater availability of Russian diesel could narrow price premiums and compress Indian refiners’ margins, he said.

The scale of the impact will depend on how much Russia can produce and export, given continuing refinery damage and export restrictions.

For India, the key variables are Chinese exports, Russian supply, regional diesel margins and freight rates. These factors will determine where Indian fuel can be sold most profitably as shifting trade flows and sanctions reshape the global diesel market.

(Edited by Tony Rai)

items.title: Bergs stuns Alcaraz in Shanghai as Zverev claims year-end top ranking
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Seven-times Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz suffered a shock 7-5 7-6(4) defeat by unseeded Belgian Zizou Bergs in the Shanghai Masters round of 32 on Monday, a result that also confirmed Alexander Zverev as the ATP's year-end world number one.
items.body:
Seven-times Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz suffered a shock 7-5 7-6(4) defeat by unseeded Belgian Zizou Bergs in the Shanghai Masters round of 32 on Monday, a result that also confirmed Alexander Zverev as the ATP's year-end world number one.
Fresh from defending his [USN:L1N45S0G0 TEXT:"Japan Open"] title and building momentum after a wrist injury that sidelined him for nearly five months, Alcaraz never found his rhythm in a scrappy two-hour, two-minute contest.
The second-seeded Spaniard joined 24-times Grand Slam champion [USN:L1N45V0DT TEXT:"Novak Djokovic"] and US Open runner-up [USN:L4N45X01T TEXT:"Ben Shelton"] among the high-profile casualties at the ATP Masters 1000 event.
Bergs produced a composed all-court performance, thriving in the quick conditions as the 27-year-old broke Alcaraz's serve three times to clinch the biggest victory of his career.
Bergs had lost their only previous meeting, falling to Alcaraz in the last 16 of last year's Japan Open, but showed no signs of intimidation as he outplayed the 23-year-old in key moments.
"I often have too much respect for these guys, which is part of my culture and I'm proud of that. But it gets a little bit in the way when you have to play them...," Bergs said.
"The more experience you have practising against them and playing matches, the more it becomes the new standard a little bit. To have this moment, for me it is a little bit of a relief. I feel like now I really can win against these guys..."
Alcaraz conceded he was below his best.
"I didn't play the way that I wanted to play. A lot of mistakes. I didn't find a good position on the return," Alcaraz said.
"Obviously, credit to him. I would say he served really well.
"But when I got into the rhythm, when I got into the point, I made a lot of mistakes. I wasn't feeling comfortable with my shots. So, I'm really disappointed with today's match because I didn't find the solution. I just made a lot of unforced errors."
'DREAM COME TRUE' The upset also guaranteed French Open and US Open champion Zverev, 29, the ATP's year-end world number one ranking, making him the first German and the oldest first-time player to achieve the feat.
Zverev's rise to year-end number one was aided by the absence of five-times Grand Slam champion [USN:L1N45S0CV TEXT:"Jannik Sinner"], who has not played since beating the German in the Wimbledon final in July due to a knee injury and will miss the rest of the season, including the ATP Finals in Turin.
"It's been a fantastic season for me winning in Paris and New York and knowing that I will finish the year on top of the rankings is just a dream come true," said Zverev, who will face Kazakhstan's 19th seed Alexander Bublik in the round of 16 in Shanghai.
"So much work and effort have been put into achieving this goal, especially after coming back from the ankle injury (at the 2022 French Open semi-finals).
"I look forward to finishing the season in style."

items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Le pape Léon XIV sera hospitalisé mardi matin en vue d'une intervention chirurgicale visant à retirer un petit nodule situé dans l'un de ses poumons, a indiqué lundi le service de presse du Vatican.
items.body:
Le pape Léon XIV sera hospitalisé mardi matin en vue d'une intervention chirurgicale visant à retirer un petit nodule situé dans l'un de ses poumons, a indiqué lundi le service de presse du Vatican.
Tous les engagements publics du saint-père sont en conséquence annulés jusqu'au 20 octobre.
Le souverain pontife, âgé de 71 ans, a annoncé dimanche que cette excroissance à un stade précoce avait été détectée lors d'un récent bilan de santé et qu'elle était "bien circonscrite".
Le Vatican n'a pas précisé la date à laquelle l'opération du pape aurait lieu.

items.body:
Papa Leone sarà ricoverato in ospedale domani mattina in vista dell'intervento chirurgico per la rimozione di un piccolo nodulo al polmone.
Lo ha riferito l'ufficio stampa del Vaticano.
Papa Leone, 71 anni, ha detto ieri che un piccolo nodulo è stato individuato durante una recente visita di controllo, che è "ben localizzato" e in fase molto iniziale.
A causa del ricovero tutte le udienze fino al 20 ottobre sono state annullate, secondo quanto riferito dal Vaticano in serata.

Oct 12 : Italian Giulio Ciccone has signed a three-year contract with Pinarello Q36.5, the Swiss team said on Monday, after the 31-year-old mutually parted ways with Lidl-Trek after eight seasons.
Ciccone's last race in the Lidl-Trek colours ended with a third-placed finish in Saturday's Giro di Lombardia, after the team announced his departure on the eve of the race despite still having three years left on his contract.
"After eight years with the same team, this is a big decision, but one I genuinely wanted to make," Ciccone said in a Pinarello Q36.5 statement.
"I feel I still have a lot to give, and I needed a new challenge, fresh motivation and an environment where I could feel at home."

• The deal value includes up to $150 million in earn-outs tied to Elisity's performance, it added

items.title: US immigration authorities raid Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar's home
items.author: Nolan Mccaskill, Andrew Goudsward, Doina Chiacu
items.creator: Nolan Mccaskill, Andrew Goudsward, Doina Chiacu
items.summary: US authorities conducted a predawn raid on Monday on the Washington-area home of Democratic US Representative Ilhan Omar of Minnesota, an outspoken critic of Donald Trump who has been the target of political insults by the Republican president, as part of an ongoing investigation, the Justice Department said.
items.body:
US authorities conducted a predawn raid on Monday on the Washington-area home of Democratic US Representative Ilhan Omar of Minnesota, an outspoken critic of Donald Trump who has been the target of political insults by the Republican president, as part of an ongoing investigation, the Justice Department said.
A person familiar with the investigation said it is related to alleged immigration fraud, and part of the probe concerns the Somali-born lawmaker's immigration paperwork, which was filled out by her late father when she was a child.
Omar wrote in a social media post that the US government is being weaponized to target a political enemy of the president.
"For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns," Omar said. "This is just the latest escalation in his campaign of political intimidation. I will not be silenced."
Other Democrats accused Trump and his administration of abuse of power. Omar, 44, is seeking a fifth two-year term in the US House of Representatives in the midterm elections on November 3.
In announcing the raid, a Justice Department spokesperson said: "Today in the Washington, DC area, Homeland Security Investigations executed a judicially authorized search warrant secured by the Department of Justice. This enforcement action is part of an ongoing federal investigation."
Homeland Security Investigations is part of US Immigration and Customs Enforcement, or ICE.
Tom Homan, the Trump administration's border czar, told Fox Business Network that the Justice Department is leading the investigation with the Department of Homeland Security. Homan declined to get into the specifics of an ongoing criminal investigation.
Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, a Trump appointee, said last month that "something's gonna happen" in the investigation into Omar's family's entry into the United States.
"If we can prove that you shouldn't have been here in the first place, we'll deport you," Mullin told conservative podcaster Benny Johnson at the time.
Monday's raid was carried out a little more than three weeks before the midterms, with Trump's party seeking to retain control of Congress. Omar, a prominent progressive, represents a safe Democratic district. She won reelection in 2024 by a margin of 50 percentage points.
DEMOCRATS CONDEMN RAID In a joint statement, US House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries and other members of the party's leadership in the chamber said the raid was "deeply disturbing and raises serious questions about the" weaponization of the federal government against Trump's enemies.
Republicans have "relentlessly targeted" Omar, said Jeffries, joined by Representatives Katherine Clark and Pete Aguilar. Trump's "mass deportation machine has descended upon the home of a duly elected Member of Congress and her family," they added, and they vowed to "deliver full accountability" for what they called a "rogue abuse of power."
Minnesota Democrats also condemned the raid.
"Americans see this for what it is," Minnesota Governor Tim Walz, a Democrat, wrote on social media. "President Trump is abusing his power to go after political opponents weeks before an election."
Justice Department policy bars federal prosecutors and agents from timing any action to affect the outcome of any election or benefiting a candidate or political party. The department has historically avoided taking investigative steps against political candidates within about 60 days of an election.
INVESTIGATIONS OF TRUMP CRITICS The Justice Department during Trump's second term in office has investigated and brought charges against a range of Trump's perceived political enemies.
It has charged former FBI Director James Comey, New York state Attorney General Letitia James and Trump's former national security adviser turned critic John Bolton. It also has investigated Democratic lawmakers who urged the US military not to follow illegal orders, Democratic Senator Adam Schiff and Federal Reserve officials Jerome Powell and Lisa Cook.
The case against James and one of two brought against Comey were thrown out by a federal judge. Bolton pleaded guilty and is scheduled to be sentenced later this month. Grand juries and federal judges have stymied several other probes.
'CREEPY OBSESSION' Omar has faced political insults from Trump, who has [USN:L1N45U12W TEXT:"cast"] the Somali American community as a threat to Minnesota in a burst of anti-Somali and anti-Muslim rhetoric. Omar has called Trump's focus on her an "unhealthy and creepy obsession."
Last week, Trump called Michigan's Democratic nominee for US Senate — Abdul El-Sayed, who is Muslim — a "RADICAL Extremist" and "Terrorist Sympathizer" while offering support for El-Sayed's Republican opponent, Mike Rogers.
Civil rights advocates have criticized Trump's rhetoric toward minorities and immigrants, including when he previously called Somalis "garbage."
Trump in February said that Omar and Democratic Representative Rashida Tlaib of Michigan, who is also Muslim, should be "institutionalized" and sent back to "where they came from." Both lawmakers had criticized Trump during his State of the Union address as he touted his administration's hard-line immigration crackdown and its immigration enforcement actions.
Omar has said she and her family have faced death threats, which she attributes to "hateful political rhetoric," especially from Trump.
Last month, a Minnesota man who squirted vinegar on Omar [USN:L6N4591B6 TEXT:"was sentenced"] to one year and two months in prison after pleading guilty to assaulting a federal official. Anthony James Kazmierczak admitted to attacking Omar because he disagreed with her progressive political views.

GENEVA: Deep funding shortfalls are forcing the UN refugee agency to make painful cuts across its humanitarian operations worldwide, and there are limits to how much restructuring can offset shrinking donor support, its chief said on Monday (Oct 12).
UNHCR has secured only US$3 billion, or 35 per cent of the US$8.5 billion in funding it requires for 2026, High Commissioner Barham Salih told the agency's executive committee at a meeting in Geneva.
The shortfall follows aid cuts by countries including the United States under President Donald Trump at a time of record global displacement.
Funding for next year remains uncertain although the expected figure of around $2.68 billion could improve after a UNHCR donor pledging conference in December, Salih said.

UNHCR has launched one of its largest restructurings in the agency's history because of the budget squeeze, with Salih saying its workforce had been reduced since 2024 from 20,000 employees to just under 12,000.
"Protection has a floor. Below it, the system does not simply become smaller. The protection we can provide begins to fail," he said.
Salih cautioned that restructuring could not compensate indefinitely for lower funding, and that the funding crisis was already having tangible consequences for refugees and humanitarian partners.
"There is a difference between doing more with less and being asked to do the impossible," he said.

Related:

IN FOCUS: 'I cannot go back' - Myanmar refugees fear repatriation as country gets cosier with Malaysia, Thailand

Number of forcibly displaced people dips to 118 million: UN

JOB CUTS UNHCR is seeking to preserve frontline operations by cutting jobs at its Geneva headquarters and worldwide regional offices, with 88 per cent of staff remaining outside headquarters, Salih said.
About 95 per cent of the staff doing protection work, such as registering refugees and providing legal assistance, and helping refugees find longer-term solutions, such as returning home safely, have been retained in field locations, he said. 
He cited several examples of programmes under threat. 
In Chad, he said, insufficient funding risks disrupting specialised medical care and legal assistance for more than 50,000 survivors of conflict-related sexual violence who fled neighbouring Sudan. 
In Ethiopia, refugee registration had been suspended for tens of thousands of refugees from South Sudan and Eritrea, he said.
Colombia has raised concerns on behalf of Latin American countries that their region is being disproportionately impacted. 
The Americas, which include the US, Canada, Latin America and the Caribbean, face a budget reduction of 32 per cent in 2027 compared to this year, or about $485 million — the largest budget reduction of any region — while the number of forcibly displaced and stateless people in the Americas is projected to increase by 4 per cent to about 24.5 million people in 2027, Salih said.

items.title: ＥＵのＨＶ輸入上限枠、中国ＥＶ各社に打撃　欧州現地生産加速へ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［上海／北京　１２日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［上海／北京　１２日　ロイター］ - 中国が欧州連合（ＥＵ）向けのハイブリッド車（ＨＶ）輸出を抑えることに同意した。国内販売の伸びが鈍る中、中国の電気自動車（ＥＶ）メーカーにとって新たな打撃になる。

中国商務省は１２日、この取り決めで輸出は今後も増やせるとし、中国には他のどの輸入元に割り当てられる枠よりも小さくない数量枠が保証されると表明した。

中国自動車各社は、ＥＵの中国製ＥＶに課す関税の対象外であるＨＶの輸出を増やしてきた。中国税関のデータによると、２０２６年上半期のＥＵ向けＨＶ輸出額は７５億ドルと、前年同期（２５億ドル）の３倍だった。

ジェフリーズによると、上海汽車集団（ＳＡＩＣ）、比亜迪（ＢＹＤ）、奇瑞汽車の３社が、ＥＵで販売される中国製ＨＶの９割超（台数ベース）を占める。３社の欧州販売では、半分以上がＨＶとなっている。

シュミット・オートモーティブ・リサーチによると、欧州ＥＶ市場での中国ブランドのシェアは２６年第２・四半期に過去最高の１５％となった。２４年第１・四半期は９．５％だった。ＰＨＥＶ市場でも中国製のシェアは４分の１を超え、２４年初めのわずか１．７％から急拡大した。

＜現地生産加速へ＞

仏ルノーのフランソワ・プロボ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は１２日、中国製ＨＶの輸入急増は欧州にとって持続可能ではないと述べた。一方で、今回の合意は貿易戦争よりは望ましいとし、通商関係を「賢明に」管理する必要があると指摘した。

投資家はおおむね、今回の合意を貿易摩擦の緩和と受け止め、中国製ＨＶへの関税が当面は見送られる兆しとみている。

シティのアナリストは、実施ルール、数量上限、最低価格などは、今後さらなる協議が必要だが、とりあえずリスクが緩和したと指摘した。

中国の自動車業界に詳しいコンサルタントのマイケル・ダン氏は「中国が合意を守るのか、それとも抜け道や一時的な関税免除を見つけるのか、見ていきたい」と述べた。

アナリストらは、数量枠の制度が始まる前に輸出を前倒しする動きが出る可能性があるが、合意は最終的に、中国の自動車メーカーによる欧州での現地生産を加速させる可能性があるとみる。

上海のコンサルティング会社オートモビリティの創業者、ビル・ルッソ氏は「これで、中国の自動車メーカーが欧州で生産する動機は強まるだろう」と述べた。

Surfing hotspots around the world are more vulnerable to climate change, says new study

The research analysed 57 surf breaks across eight countries to arrive at its findings. Each of the sites selected is incorporated into a World Surfing Reserve.

Purvi Rajpuria

12 October, 2026 04:43 pm IST

New Delhi: Many of the most prominent surf breaks across the world are vulnerable to climate change, even as the degree and type of vulnerability differ widely, a recent study found. 

The study, titled ‘ Globally significant surf breaks are vulnerable to climate change ’, was co-authored by Dan R Reineman of California State University Channel Islands, along with researchers from Save The Waves Coalition and World Surfing Reserves . 

The research analysed 57 surf breaks across eight countries to arrive at its findings. Each of the sites selected is incorporated into a World Surfing Reserve (WSR)—“a status applied for by local stakeholders and designated by an international non-profit organization based on each site’s cultural, historical, and environmental significance for surfing,” the study explains.

Show Full Article

These surf breaks, the research found, are vulnerable to climate change, due to changing tide levels, hardened shorelines caused by manmade structures, and shifting sands. Surf breaks rated at most risk include Croyde beach in north Devon, UK, and Oriente Salvaje in El Salvador. 

What are surf breaks?
Dan Reineman, a co-author of the study, pointed to the several factors that come together to form a surf break. “Surf breaks are incredibly unique oceanographic phenomena – a confluence of all these factors that fit together just right to make the wave happen – and so those processes are really sensitive,” he said .

Some of these factors include swell direction, tide, and intricate combinations of sea-floor shape. Climate change, global warming, and changing rainfall patterns can affect any of these factors, hampering the delicate balance of surf breaks and thus destroying the wave. 

Significantly, the study found that coastlines that were more natural and less populated by manmade structures could adapt better to the changes caused by climate change. These coastlines were able to adapt by shifting inland and relocating sediments. Construction of features such as sea walls, jetties and groynes made the beaches and waves less resilient, Reineman said .

Also read: Mamdani has a new target. Subscriptions that make cancellations difficult

Affects local economy at large
Climate change-related vulnerability matters not only to surfers, but also to the local people who depend on the multi-billion-dollar surf economy that exists in these sites. 

Adam Hall, a co-founder of the North Devon WSR, was one of the local surfers who contributed to the study. Explaining the significance of surfing to the local economy, he said , “Surfers will come throughout the year. They fill up the pubs, restaurants and car parks when the swells are good in January, February and March, where if you go to any other tourist destination that doesn’t have surf, they’re dead on their knees.”

Many of these sites often have little else in terms of local economy. 

Local surfers also played a key role in guiding the research. Trent Hodges, a co-author of the study and a senior programmes manager at Save the Waves Coalition, said , “We learned directly from the local surfers how they are seeing their waves change. It’s a canary in the coalmine too – when a wave changes, that often means the beach is changing, and everybody enjoys the beach.”

The study also hypothesises that similar risks could affect other surf breaks, not included in the present research, and encourages other local people and organisations to assess their vulnerability. 

(Edited by Ratan Priya)

Oct 12 : Norway's data protection authority has fined Microsoft's adtech unit Xandr 92 million crowns ($9.61 million) for unlawfully relaying Grindr users' sensitive data to thousands of advertisers, it said on Monday.
Xandr relayed data revealing the sexual orientation of users of Grindr, a dating app for LGBTQIA+ people, to companies in automated ad auctions from July 2018 to April 2020.
It is the biggest fine the Norwegian authority has issued, and targets the advertising middlemen rather than the app itself. The regulator said companies that traded in people's data could not pass the blame to others.
The data protection authority fined Grindr 65 million crowns over the same breaches in 2021.

The fine was based on Xandr's revenue, not Microsoft's, which did not own the unit at the time. Xandr has three weeks to appeal.
Xandr said it assumed Grindr had obtained users' consent and never checked, the data protection authority said. It rejected that argument and ruled Xandr shared legal responsibility with Grindr. 
Microsoft said the privacy of users was a top priority.
"This investigation and decision focused on conduct that predates Microsoft's acquisition of Xandr, and in that time the interpretation and application of legal standards and practices has continued to evolve. We are reviewing the decision and assessing our options," it said.
The case began with a 2020 complaint by the Norwegian Consumer Council, whose research exposed how apps shared user data, and Austrian data privacy organisation noyb, which called the decision "a valuable precedent".  
($1 = 9.5704 Norwegian crowns)

items.title: FTSE 100 ends higher as financial, medical stocks offset crude price hit
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Britain's FTSE 100 edged higher on Monday, buoyed by financials and medical equipment stocks as investors looked ahead to crucial US inflation data and UK GDP readings due this week for fresh insight into the economic outlook.
items.body:
Britain's FTSE 100 edged higher on Monday, buoyed by financials and medical equipment stocks as investors looked ahead to crucial US inflation data and UK GDP readings due this week for fresh insight into the economic outlook.
The blue-chip FTSE 100 index (.FTSE) rose nearly 1% to 10,656.28 points, while the midcap FTSE 250 (.FTMC) climbed 0.47%.
Oil prices jumped 2% to $106.76 a barrel, hovering near two-week peaks, as attacks on Saudi Arabia outweighed prospects of higher supplies from Russia and a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire on energy facilities
Attention will also be on UK Finance Minister John Healey's meetings with foreign counterparts on his first trip to the International Monetary Fund's annual meetings this week
Healey faces pressure ahead of his [USN:L8N45X047 TEXT:"first annual budget on October 28"], with higher borrowing costs and an estimated £36 billion fiscal gap to address
"I will work with our international partners  to keep trade moving, support families and businesses, and make Britain's economy stronger and more resilient," Healey said ahead of his address at the IMF meetings later this week
Upper Crust chain owner SSP Group (SSPG.L) shares fell 2.2% after brokerage [USN:L6N45Y0LK TEXT:"Berenberg cut target price"] to £225 from £245
Burberry (BRBY.L) shares rose 1.9% after retailer Frasers (FRAS.L) increased its stake in the luxury brand to 7.42% from 6.32%
Financial stocks (.FTNMX301010) were among top gainers: HSBC Holdings (HSBA.L) , Standard Life (SDLF.L) , Lloyds Banking Group , Barclays (BARC.L) , NatWest (NWG.L) , Standard Chartered (STAN.L) gain between 1.7% and 2.3%
Medical equipment and services (.FTNMX201020) shares rose 2.75%
Market participants are awaiting US inflation data due on Wednesday, while UK GDP figures for August are scheduled for release on Thursday

items.title: Oro cae desde máximo de una semana por fortaleza del dólar y avance del petróleo
items.author: Vishak Mathew
items.creator: Vishak Mathew
items.summary: Los precios del oro cayeron el lunes tras alcanzar un máximo de una semana a primera hora de la sesión, ya que la fortaleza del dólar y el alza del petróleo lastraron al metal precioso.
items.body:
Los precios del oro cayeron el lunes tras alcanzar un máximo de una semana a primera hora de la sesión, ya que la fortaleza del dólar y el alza del petróleo lastraron al metal precioso.
* Los inversionistas, en tanto, esperan los datos de inflación de Estados Unidos, que podrían modificar las expectativas sobre la trayectoria de las tasas de interés.
* El oro al contado bajaba un 0,6% a 4.169,10 dólares por onza a las 1745 GMT, tras alcanzar su nivel más alto desde el 2 de octubre a primera hora de la sesión. Los futuros del oro estadounidense con entrega en diciembre caían un 0,6% a 4.190,60 dólares por onza.
* "Estamos observando cierta presión vendedora sobre el oro porque el dólar se encuentra cerca de su máximo en un año y medio", afirmó Jim Wyckoff, analista de mercado de American Gold Exchange.
* La escalada del conflicto en Oriente Medio mantuvo a los inversores en vilo a la espera de los datos clave sobre la inflación en Estados Unidos de esta semana, que influirán en la política monetaria.
* El reporte del Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) de Estados Unidos se publicará el miércoles, seguido del Índice de Precios al Productor (IPP) y de los datos de ventas al por menor el jueves.
* Los mercados han reducido sus apuestas por una subida de tasas de interés de la Fed este mes; según la herramienta FedWatch de CME, los operadores descuentan un 18% de probabilidades de que se produzca una subida este mes, aunque siguen viendo un 88% de probabilidades de que se produzca una subida en diciembre.
* En un entorno de tasas de interés elevadas, los inversionistas tienden a preferir los activos que generan rendimiento frente al oro.
* El petróleo subió a cerca de máximos de dos semanas ya que los ataques contra Arabia Saudita eclipsaron la posibilidad de un aumento de la oferta en el mercado, después de que el presidente Donald Trump, acogiera con satisfacción las nuevas exportaciones rusas de gasóleo y el alto el fuego energético entre Rusia y Ucrania.
* Entre otros metales preciosos, la plata al contado caía un 1% a 60,22 dólares por onza; el platino bajaba un 0,2% a 1.684,20 dólares por onza; y el paladio caía un 0,5% a 1.141,90 dólares por onza.

items.title: Jury selected for actor Russell Brand's UK trial over sex crimes allegations
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Jury selection took place on Monday for the trial of British actor and comedian Russell Brand over alleged historical crimes including rape and other sexual offences.
items.body:
Jury selection took place on Monday for the trial of British actor and comedian Russell Brand over alleged historical crimes including rape and other sexual offences.
Brand, 51, once one of Britain's most high-profile broadcasters and former husband of US singer Katy Perry, faces three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of indecent assault relating to six women from 1999 to 2009.
Brand has denied all the accusations. He arrived at London's Southwark Crown Court wearing sunglasses and accompanied by his wife. During the hearing he sat in the dock, mostly staring straight ahead or with his eyes closed.
"We are about to start the trial of one Mr Russell Brand," the judge Joel Bennathan told potential jurors. "Many of you will have heard of him."
The judge excluded those who said they had watched a documentary aired about three years ago or had read a long newspaper article from the same time in which allegations of sexual misconduct were made against Brand.
"Those are allegations he firmly denies," the judge said.
He later told those who had been initially selected: "The defendant is clearly someone very well known. You absolutely must not carry out any research at all about this defendant Russell Brand."
The trial is expected to last about six weeks, Bennathan said, with the jurors formally sworn in on Tuesday while prosecutors will open their case later in the week.
The comedian, known for his flamboyant style and appearance, was a regular on British television screens in the 2000s and also worked as a radio presenter for the BBC.
He went on to star in a number of films including "Get Him to the Greek" in 2010, the same year he married Perry. They divorced in 2012 after 14 months of marriage.
More recently Brand has largely appeared on online programmes, with content often focused on US politics, religion and free speech.
