items.title: Aluminio repunta desde mínimo de ocho meses y el cobre toca máximo de dos semanas
items.author: Polina Devitt
items.creator: Polina Devitt
items.summary: Los precios del aluminio tocaron el lunes un mínimo de ocho meses, ya que la fortaleza del dólar ejerció presión sobre el ánimo de los inversores, mientras que el cobre tocó un pico de más de dos semanas por preocupaciones sobre las interrupciones en el suministro de las minas.
items.body:
Los precios del aluminio tocaron el lunes un mínimo de ocho meses, ya que la fortaleza del dólar ejerció presión sobre el ánimo de los inversores, mientras que el cobre tocó un pico de más de dos semanas por preocupaciones sobre las interrupciones en el suministro de las minas.
* El contrato de referencia del aluminio a tres meses en la Bolsa de Metales de Londres (LME) ganó un 0,2%, a 3.054 dólares por tonelada, a las 1604 GMT, tras hallar soporte en los 3.023 dólares, su nivel más bajo desde el 13 de febrero, más temprano en la sesión.
* El dólar alcanzó su nivel más alto desde abril de 2025 a la espera de los datos clave sobre la inflación en Estados Unidos que se publicarán más adelante esta semana y que podrían marcar las perspectivas de las tasas de interés.
* El aluminio ha caído un 19% desde que tocó un máximo de cuatro años en junio, según se disipaban las preocupaciones sobre las interrupciones del suministro procedentes de la región del golfo Pérsico y crecían las expectativas de una mayor capacidad de producción en Indonesia.
* Aunque los bajos niveles de existencias visibles siguen respaldando los precios, es probable que la aceleración del crecimiento de la oferta fuera de China empuje al mercado mundial a un superávit de 1,8 millones de toneladas en 2027, frente al déficit de 941.000 toneladas de este año, según Citi.
* Por su parte, el cobre en la LME subió un 0,5%, a 14.616 dólares por tonelada, tras alcanzar los 14.688 dólares, su cota más elevada desde el 25 de septiembre.
* Las preocupaciones sobre el suministro se vieron avivadas por una suspensión parcial en la mina El Teniente de Codelco, en Chile, tras un alud que causó la muerte de dos trabajadores el domingo. La huelga en la mina Centinela de Antofagasta, también en Chile, continúa, y está previsto que las negociaciones se reanuden el martes.
* En otros metales básicos, el zinc cayó un 1,2%, a 3.757,5 dólares; el níquel cedió un 0,1%, a 15.595 dólares, tras tocar su mínimo desde fines de diciembre, a 15.500 dólares; el plomo bajó un 0,2%, a 1.883,5 dólares; y el estaño sumó un 0,4%, a 53.155 dólares.

items.title: Australia need six wickets on final day to win first test
items.author: Mark Gleeson
items.creator: Mark Gleeson
items.summary: Australia's Matt Renshaw played a leading role to leave his side needing six wickets on the last day of the first test to beat South Africa as the hosts were 102-4 at the close of play at Kingsmead on Monday.
items.body:
Australia's Matt Renshaw played a leading role to leave his side needing six wickets on the last day of the first test to beat South Africa as the hosts were 102-4 at the close of play at Kingsmead on Monday.
Set 421 runs to win after Australia declared their second innings on 314-6, South Africa saw opener Ryan Rickelton, David Bedingham, captain Temba Bavuma and Tristan Stubbs all dismissed before stumps with part time spinner Renshaw weighing in with his first test wicket as his dream performance continued.
Aiden Markram (45 not out) and Wiaan Mulder, unbeaten on five, will resume on the final morning, needing to lead a stoic rearguard action if the home side are to avoid defeat.
"We gave up a couple of soft wickets again but the application Aiden showed is what we are looking forward tomorrow," said veteran spinner Keshav Maharaj.
Rickelton’s place in the test side looks under threat after another early dismissal. He was out for a duck after three balls of the first innings and scored two on Monday before an attempted pull shot saw him edge Josh Hazlewood's rising delivery to wicketkeeper Alex Carey.
Bedingham was the second wicket to fall, making 46 before being trapped lbw by Hazlewood and ending a patient 66-run partnership with Markram, while Bavuma scored a single run, prodding at Renshaw's off spin and being caught bat-pad at short leg.
Stubbs also made one, getting a thick edge to captain Pat Cummins' delivery with another example of the poor shot selection that has dogged South Africa's batting.
"It's been a good last two days for us," said Australia's Beau Webster. "We've still got a job to do tomorrow but given ourselves a great chance."
RED-HOT BATTING FORM Earlier, Renshaw continued his red-hot batting form to allow his side to declare at tea, picking up where he left off in the first innings when he scored 190 of Australia's 390 runs.
The 30-year-old Queenslander continued to dominate the home bowlers, scoring 82 in the second innings before a controversial caught and bowled from Maharaj ended his contribution.
It was the top score for Australia, who accelerated their run accumulation in a bid to give themselves time to put South Africa into bat and chase down the 10 wickets required for victory.
They resumed on 33-0 and scored 141 runs in a fast-moving first session for the loss of four wickets and a further 140 in the afternoon.
CAPTAIN CUMMINS IN WHIRLWIND BATTING DISPLAY Opener Nic Maddinson, who made a duck in the first innings on his return after a decade out of test cricket, played some expansive shots before Anrich Nortje clean bowled him for 48, and there were useful contributions from Beau Webster, 39 not out, and Cummins, who bludgeoned four sixes in his whirlwind 12-ball 32.
Travis Head's 11 runs at the top of the Australia innings and 37 again from Marnus Labuschagne did not help their individual causes, although Labuschagne's 53-run partnership with Steve Smith (27) for the third wicket did accelerate the run rate and put Australia into an advantageous position.
Smith was struck on the helmet by Nortje and is being assessed under concussion protocols. He batted on after the hit but did not join the rest of the Australian team on the field at the start of South Africa's chase and could be a doubt for the second test, which starts in Gqeberha on Sunday.

items.title: Papa León ingresará el martes al hospital para someterse a intervención quirúrgica: Vaticano
items.author: Joshua McElwee
items.creator: Joshua McElwee
items.summary: El Papa León ingresará en el hospital el martes para someterse a una intervención quirúrgica destinada a extirpar un pequeño nódulo detectado en un pulmón, informó el Vaticano, mientras el pontífice mantuvo una apretada agenda el lunes, celebrando por la mañana siete reuniones programadas con antelación.
items.body:
El Papa León ingresará en el hospital el martes para someterse a una intervención quirúrgica destinada a extirpar un pequeño nódulo detectado en un pulmón, informó el Vaticano, mientras el pontífice mantuvo una apretada agenda el lunes, celebrando por la mañana siete reuniones programadas con antelación.
León, de 71 años, declaró el domingo que el nódulo se había detectado en un chequeo reciente, que estaba "bien delimitado" y que se había detectado a tiempo.
El nódulo se detectó durante un chequeo médico rutinario, informó la oficina de prensa del Vaticano a primera hora del lunes, antes de confirmar que se espera que el Papa sea ingresado a última hora de la mañana del martes, antes de la intervención quirúrgica.
No se especificó cuándo tendría lugar la operación propiamente dicha.
El comunicado habitual sobre la agenda diaria del Papa, publicado el lunes al mediodía (1000 GMT), indicaba que se había reunido esa mañana con obispos visitantes de Argentina, Nicaragua y Estados Unidos, entre otros.
En una reunión celebrada el lunes en el Vaticano con miembros de una organización benéfica con sede en Roma, el Papa habló con voz firme, agradeciéndoles su labor.
León ha cancelado todos los actos públicos que tenía programados hasta el 20 de octubre, informó el Vaticano.
León, elegido papa por los cardenales de todo el mundo en mayo de 2025, es relativamente joven para ser un líder de la Iglesia. Le gustan los deportes, incluido el tenis, y no se sabe que sea fumador ni que haya tenido problemas de salud anteriormente.
El Vaticano ha indicado que se espera que la recuperación del Papa dure aproximadamente una semana.
Un nódulo pulmonar es una pequeña lesión localizada que puede ser benigna. Según la Sociedad Torácica Americana, menos del 5% de los nódulos pulmonares resultan ser cancerosos, aunque el riesgo aumenta con la edad, el tamaño y otros factores como el tabaquismo.
El doctor Federico Venuto, jefe de cirugía torácica del hospital Policlínico Umberto I de Roma, explicó que las intervenciones quirúrgicas para extirpar nódulos pulmonares suelen ser mínimamente invasivas y, en ocasiones, pueden implicar el uso de un tubo con cámara delgada denominado toracoscopio.
"La tasa de complicaciones es extremadamente baja", declaró a Reuters.
León, líder de una Iglesia que cuenta con 1.400 millones de fieles, tenía varias citas públicas en su agenda para esta semana, incluida una misa en la Plaza de San Pedro el miércoles por la mañana.
El Vaticano no ha confirmado si la misa, que cierra una asamblea de obispos de una semana de duración, aún se celebrará. Aunque el Papa ingresará en el hospital el martes, la misa podría ser oficiada por un cardenal del Vaticano.
León, de 71 años, dijo el domingo que el pequeño nódulo se había detectado en un chequeo reciente, que estaba "bien delimitado" y que se había encontrado a tiempo. El nódulo se detectó durante un chequeo médico rutinario, confirmó el lunes la oficina de prensa del Vaticano.

items.title: What is the Putin-Trump diesel deal, and can it ease US fuel price pain?
items.summary: Trump has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel exports to lower US prices, but supply limits, tanker sanctions and refinery damage could curb the impact ahead of midterm polls ...
items.body:
Home / World News / What is the Putin-Trump diesel deal, and can it ease US fuel price pain?

What is the Putin-Trump diesel deal, and can it ease US fuel price pain? Trump has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel exports to lower US prices, but supply limits, tanker sanctions and refinery damage could curb the impact ahead of midterm polls

President Donald Trump (Photo:PTI)

Reuters 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 12 2026 | 10:48 PM IST

Listen to This Article

US President Donald Trump has stepped up his efforts to lower US diesel prices by lifting sanctions on Russian diesel exports and announcing a ceasefire on energy infrastructure between Russia and Ukraine.
  Soaring US diesel prices are hurting US truckers and farmers, and are a concern for voters and political parties ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.
  US prices were down 0.5 per cent on Monday following Trump's announcements.
  How much difference will Russia's release make?
  Trump said on Friday that Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 tonnes (2.25 million barrels) of diesel to US and global markets.
Also Read

Russia violated energy ceasefire announced by Trump, says Zelenskyy

Russia to supply diesel to US, global markets: What it means for India

EU sanctions nearly 1,600 Russians and firms over drone, missile parts

US Senators question legality of Trump's deal to allow Russian oil imports

Ukrainian Prez risks rupture with Trump as US midterms pressure mounts

  That is less than a day's supply for the US transport sector alone, according to US Energy Information Administration data, which show daily use of around 2.94 million barrels.
 

  Trump said Russia would supply another 500,000 tonnes in November and a further 1 million tonnes "immediately thereafter", which is less than four days' demand for US transport.
  What hurdles might there be?
  The US has lifted sanctions on Russian diesel exports, but it remains unclear which tankers could be used to export the fuel, given sanctions on many of them, and what condition Russian refineries are in following recent Ukrainian attacks on them.
  How much can Russia export?
  Russia was capable of exporting about 100,000 tonnes of diesel a day before Ukrainian drone attacks on refineries began in 2024.
  In light of damage to its refineries, Russia banned diesel exports from July to meet domestic demand and extended that ban to countries without bilateral agreements until October 31, while sustaining steady exports to "friendly" states, mostly in Central Asia.

  If Ukraine halts attacks on Russian refineries, Russia would be capable of meeting the initial request from Trump for 300,000 tonnes of diesel exports, according to industry sources.
  Russia could produce 300,000 tonnes of diesel this month if a large oil refinery hit by drones in the European part of the country were to restart, the sources said.
  Will more diesel exports help Russia's economy?
  According to Russian President Vladimir Putin, Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries cost Russia's economy 1 per cent of gross domestic product, which is around $26.6 billion, according to Reuters calculations.
  Exports of 300,000 tonnes of diesel would fetch roughly $400 million, of which a small portion would go to Russia's state budget. Russia taxes mostly oil output, not oil and fuel exports.

  Russia has around 30 large oil refineries, while none are functioning in Ukraine.
  What’s been the reaction to Trump's announcements?
  Moscow said on Saturday it had partially lifted the ban on diesel exports in place since July with immediate effect.
  Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Trump's diesel supply deal with Russia would embolden Moscow's attacks on Ukraine and cost more lives.
  US lawmakers also criticised the move, including one of Trump's fellow Republicans, Representative Don Bacon, who said it was time to apply more sanctions that Congress had recently passed, not lift them.
  British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said his country would strengthen its sanctions on Russia. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul restated Berlin's support for Ukraine’s leader after Trump called for his removal, and called for more pressure to be put on Russia to resume peace talks.

  The Kremlin said on Monday the talks were continuing on the ceasefire, while declining to comment on whether it relates only to oil refineries.
  China's impact on diesel
  China is set to resume refined fuel exports after a brief halt during the Golden Week holiday, Reuters reported.
  However, its approved October exports of diesel, petrol and jet fuel, at around 3.7 million tonnes, are down sharply from a year earlier and lower than the more than 4 million tonnes approved for September.
  Why have diesel prices been so tight?
  In addition to Russian export challenges, the Iran war has curbed supply from Gulf producers.
  IEA spurring more supply

  The Group of Seven nations agreed recently to release fuel from their strategic reserves, coordinated by the International Energy Agency.
  The 32-nation IEA coordinated the world's largest emergency stocks release in March of over 400 million barrels of crude oil and products, and has recently prodded participating countries to offer any unreleased volumes to the market.

items.title: ノーベル経済学賞、米大教授2人に　経済安定化の研究
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ストックホルム　１２日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ストックホルム　１２日　ロイター］ - スウェーデン王立科学アカデミーは１２日、２０２６年のノーベル経済学賞を米スタンフォード大学のロバート・ホール教授（８３）と米コロンビア大学のマイケル・ウッドフォード教授（７０）に授与すると発表した。授賞理由は「マクロ経済の安定化に関するミクロ経済学的基盤」。

両氏は、効果的な安定化政策を実行する能力を向上させる新たなボトムアップ型の経済モデルを開発した。これにより、経済に打撃を与える変動の激しさを緩和できる、適切なタイミングでの財政・金融政策の実施が可能となり、世界の中央銀行や財務省で活用されている。

経済学賞選考委員会のジョン・ハスラー委員長は声明で「両氏の功績は、現在世界中の各中央銀行や政府によって使われているモデルに安定した理論的基盤を提供した」と指摘。「両氏のモデルによって、エネルギー危機や家計消費の急変動など、経済へのショックにより適切に対処できるようになった」と述べた。

両氏の重要な洞察の一つは、経済の仕組みを上から捉えるトップダウン型の理論に頼るのではなく、家計や企業がミクロのレベルで下す無数の決定を考慮して初めて経済を安定させられるという点だ。

ウッドフォード氏は会見で「当局は、経済の安定化を、経済の中にいる人々がそれをどう理解しているかとは関係なく、誰かがレバーを引いて経済を操作するだけの作業と見なすべきではない」と語った。

ウッドフォード氏によると、中銀が高騰するインフレへの対応に苦しんだ１９７０年代の石油危機とは違い、２０００年代後半の世界金融危機では、新たな枠組みが伝統的な金融政策手段を補う上で役に立った。

「すぐに追加利下げできることだけに頼るのではなく、金利政策が今後どうなりそうかをより明確に表明することが、０９年以降の政策対応の重要な部分を占めた」と述べた。

両氏の研究は、金融政策の先行きを示す、いわゆる「フォワードガイダンス」のほかにも、需要が変化しても価格の変化が遅れる「粘着的な」インフレ、「需給ギャップ（アウトプットギャップ）」といった現在使われている概念を広めた。

items.title: Bardella antisemitism dispute tests French far right's decade-long makeover
items.author: Elizabeth Pineau, Michel Rose
items.creator: Elizabeth Pineau, Michel Rose
items.summary: Joseph Martin saw his hopes of becoming a far-right National Rally (RN) lawmaker derailed in 2024 after journalists unearthed a seemingly antisemitic post.
items.body:
Joseph Martin saw his hopes of becoming a far-right National Rally (RN) lawmaker derailed in 2024 after journalists unearthed a seemingly antisemitic post.
It was RN president Jordan Bardella who initially withdrew support for [USN:L1N3UP0GG TEXT:"Martin's candidacy"], seeking to show [USN:L8N3J31HH TEXT:"zero tolerance"] for antisemitism as [USN:L8N3IN1AQ TEXT:"the party tried"] to convince voters it had shed its toxic past and was ready for top office.
So as the RN closes ranks around Bardella while he grapples with his own accusations of antisemitism – which he denies – Martin said the RN chief should be held to the same standard and step aside while the claims are investigated.
"He judged me, condemned me and excluded me from the RN," said Martin, who was eventually cleared to run after the RN agreed his post was not antisemitic. However, he lost and saw his subsequent application to represent the party in future votes rejected, essentially ending his political career.
The discrepancy between how the RN handled accusations against the two men - one the rising star of the party and the other a little-known regional candidate - raises questions about one of its most fundamental claims: that it has decisively broken with the [USN:L8N3CE2UV TEXT:"antisemitism"] that marked parts of its history.
"There's been packaging, cosmetics and strategy, but the ideas persist," said Sciences-Po university political scientist Gilles Ivaldi.
BARDELLA STANDS HIS GROUND Bardella has denied the allegations by investigative outlet Mediapart, which published purported antisemitic and conspiratorial comments he made in chats as a teenager, calling them "crude fakes" and saying he would file defamation lawsuits.
Still, the scandal represents the gravest threat yet to the 31-year-old's rapid political ascent, while also posing a headache for RN presidential candidate Marine Le Pen as she seeks to win the presidency after three failed attempts.
Le Pen, who leads polls ahead of next year's vote, has led a decade-long rebrand of the RN, while Bardella has visited Israel to show the party is free of the antisemitism for which its founder, Marine's father Jean-Marie Le Pen, was convicted.
"This affair shines a harsh light on what the National Rally really is," said Socialist lawmaker Guillaume Garot. However, he also acknowledged the controversy was competing for attention with a long list of voter concerns, from high school protests and a weak economy to geopolitics.
ALLEGATIONS MAY HURT LE PEN IN RUN-OFF VOTE The RN has rallied to Bardella's defence, while also playing down the scandal. "I think it has absolutely no impact on the ground whatsoever," Le Pen aide Renaud Labaye told Reuters.
Some 74% of the French believe the messages are problematic if true, according to an IFOP poll for LCI TV, but only 21% say their opinion of Bardella has deteriorated.
Bardella struck a defiant tone when challenged by a Mediapart journalist at a press conference last week.
"Your little operation doesn't seem to be cutting through," he said. "You'd have loved to see me on my knees, but you clearly don't know me very well."
Ivaldi said the RN's most loyal voters were unlikely to abandon the party as their priorities were purchasing power, energy prices, immigration and crime. But the scandal could hurt Le Pen in a run-off, when victory would depend on attracting conservative voters beyond the RN's traditional base.
"If there is an impact, it is more likely to be among second-round voters, particularly those who pay closer attention to the RN's ideological profile," he said.
INTERNAL TENSIONS The controversy comes at a delicate moment in the relationship between Le Pen and her protege Bardella, who had been the party's de facto presidential candidate until a Paris appeals court cleared her to run in a [USN:L6N4380IL TEXT:"shock July ruling"].
Bardella had increasingly asserted his independence in the run-up to that verdict, and party officials said frictions have since grown, including over the RN's rapprochement with Le Pen's niece, Marion Maréchal, an anti-abortion firebrand and potential Bardella rival.
RN Senator Joshua Hochart played down the tensions but said Bardella was willing to make his disagreement known.
"Bardella isn't just Marine Le Pen's protégé. His views count and he's right to say when something isn't working," he said.
Although Le Pen has backed Bardella over the antisemitism claims, political rivals and analysts say he has been weakened.
"The case complicates Marine Le Pen's campaign," Ivaldi said. "He is no longer the major asset he was for her."
And in a party with a long history of sidelining ambitious politicians from outside the Le Pen clan, Bardella's future remains uncertain, Ivaldi said.
Eric Zemmour, a former presidential candidate from the extreme-right Reconquest party, was blunt about Bardella's diminished status.
"Jordan Bardella is in the process of being marginalized from the heart of the RN," he said on RTL radio on Monday, predicting he would now never become Le Pen's prime minister. "It's finished all that."

items.title: Most Americans oppose betting on elections, government events, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
items.author: Chris Prentice, Jason Lange
items.creator: Chris Prentice, Jason Lange
items.summary: Most Americans oppose using prediction markets to bet on US elections and other government actions, according to a Reuters/Ipsos opinion poll that suggests the booming markets may lack broad public support as policymakers debate how to regulate them.
items.body:
Most Americans oppose using prediction markets to bet on US elections and other government actions, according to a Reuters/Ipsos opinion poll that suggests the booming markets may lack broad public support as policymakers debate how to regulate them.
The [USN:L4N42Y0WQ TEXT:"rapidly growing prediction market industry"] led by Polymarket and Kalshi allows people to bet on a raft of events, including US elections, government policy moves and sports games, raising concerns among policymakers that the platforms are opening up new avenues for [USN:L6N44E0TQ TEXT:"insider trading"] and manipulation.
The companies say they have [USN:L4N42H1L3 TEXT:"extensive controls"] to guard against misconduct, that their markets are often better at forecasting outcomes than traditional polls, and that they [USN:L6N44L0X4 TEXT:"offer unique ways to hedge"] a range of esoteric real-world risks.
Yet a bipartisan majority of Americans is opposed to using prediction markets to bet on US elections , military actions and government policy announcements or decisions, according to the Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted September 30 through October 5.
Some 69% of Democrats and 61% of Republicans said they opposed using prediction markets to bet on election results.
Sixty-five percent of Americans opposed prediction market betting on US military actions and 63% opposed betting on government policy announcements or decisions, suggesting broad bipartisan discomfort with wagering on government affairs. Only 8% and 9%, respectively, supported such bets.
The results shed more light on popular attitudes toward the nascent industry, which is marketing heavily on social media and TV even as it faces pushback from states and from Democratic lawmakers who argue the markets are unethical, socially corrosive and could undermine national security.
"Everyone should make their own decisions about their lives," said Ronna Schmoker, 72, a Democrat from a Dallas suburb who participated in the poll. "But like anything, you have to have guardrails."
A Polymarket spokesperson said Americans don't trust traditional information sources and that prediction markets help provide unbiased, accurate information.
"It’s why more than 90% of visits to Polymarket are to view markets, not to trade," the spokesperson said. "Recognition of the public value of prediction markets is growing, but they’re still brand new to most, and it’s going to take some time for the public to learn more and see the real value."
NATIONAL SECURITY AND ELECTION FEARS HAVE STOKED DEBATE Some policymakers worry that prediction markets, which offer thousands of ways to wager on the US midterms, [USN:L6N41V1AT TEXT:"could undermine faith in"] the integrity of US democracy and enable government insiders to broadcast confidential information via their trades.
Reuters reported [USN:L6N44E0TQ TEXT:"in August"] that more than 150 accounts on Polymarket International, the company's overseas market which bars US users, may have traded on inside military information, while Kalshi [USN:L1N41514R TEXT:"has suspended candidates"] for betting on their own races.
Kalshi banned former Republican congressman George Santos, who agreed to pay $35,000 [USN:L6N43X19K TEXT:"to resolve government allegations"] of manipulative trading after he bet via Kalshi on whether he would attend the State of the Union address. Santos did not admit to the allegations and said through his attorney that he never intended to deceive anyone.
Ninety-three percent of Democrats and 89% of Republicans said it was inappropriate for members of Congress or their staff to bet on political events, while 6% and 8%, respectively, said it was appropriate.
Polymarket and Kalshi say they work closely with the authorities and routinely refer suspicious accounts, and have introduced various restrictions to mitigate misconduct.
Kalshi says it does not allow trading on military operations and bars political candidates from wagering on their own races. The Senate in April barred senators, staff and other officers from using prediction markets, and [USN:L4N4051K3 TEXT:"several Democratic lawmakers have introduced bills"] to restrict the industry.
"We see prediction markets everywhere, but don't mistake seeing millions of dollars in advertisements as a sign of growing support," said Democratic Senator Jeff Merkley of Oregon. "Folks are rightfully concerned."
The Reuters/Ipsos poll suggests many Americans are generally uneasy about increasingly commoditizing real-world events. Even betting on professional sports, a far more established activity, was opposed by 43% of respondents, while 29% supported it.
"I just don't think it's good for a society to bet on whether things will turn out a certain way," said Michael Clark, a 48-year-old conservative who lives outside Dallas and participated in the poll.
TRUMP ADMINISTRATION HAS SUPPORTED INDUSTRY GROWTH The administration of President Donald Trump, whose son Donald Trump Jr. has business ties to Kalshi and Polymarket, is pursuing federal regulations for the industry, a move states are fighting. Legal experts expect that dispute to reach the Supreme Court.
At issue is whether prediction markets facilitate trading in financial instruments or gambling, which is regulated by the states. State regulators say they are facilitating gambling and should be subject to more stringent state laws, while Trump's Commodity Futures Trading Commission has asserted jurisdiction, arguing the contracts are a type of financial product it regulates.
"By that rationale, MGM (Resorts) owns dozens of financial markets," said Glenn Rishton, a 76-year-old Republican poll respondent in Gulfport, Mississippi, referring to the casino company. "It's effectively gambling."
Three-quarters of Americans agreed, with only 8% saying using prediction markets to wager on the outcome of real-world events is not a form of gambling.
The Reuters/Ipsos poll, which was conducted online and nationwide, surveyed 4,506 US adults and had a margin of error of about two percentage points.
"Prediction markets should have the same level of regulations as gambling," said Janessa Manning, 48, a Democrat in Detroit. "Even though they pretend they aren’t gambling, they are."

items.title: Kyiv says Russia hits energy targets despite Trump ceasefire announcement
items.author: Daniel Flynn, Pavel Polityuk
items.creator: Daniel Flynn, Pavel Polityuk
items.summary: Russia hit at least six energy targets during a night and morning of deadly airstrikes across Ukraine, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday, adding this showed Moscow had no interest in an energy ceasefire announced by Donald Trump.
items.body:
Russia hit at least six energy targets during a night and morning of deadly airstrikes across Ukraine, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday, adding this showed Moscow had no interest in an energy ceasefire announced by Donald Trump.
Under pressure over high energy prices ahead of US midterm elections next month, US President Trump blindsided Kyiv and its European allies over the weekend by declaring that Ukraine and Russia had agreed not to hit each other's energy systems.
"It is increasingly evident that Russia is unwilling to accept an energy ceasefire proposed by the United States and intends to continue its terrorist air attacks against our people and communities," Zelenskiy said on X.
"This is what happens when Russia sees the prospect of higher revenues for its war machine."
In earlier comments by video link to a conference in Poland, Zelenskiy identified two of the targets as a gas facility and a petrol station, both hit by Russian drones.
Trump announced the purported energy ceasefire days after unveiling a [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"deal to buy diesel from Russia"], which Zelenskiy has criticised as a reversal of years of Western policy aimed at isolating Russia's economy.
Trump, for his part, has called on Ukrainians to unseat Zelenskiy in an election, an unusually severe exchange in a relationship between the two leaders that has been strained since Trump returned to power in 2025.
Trump's announcement was the second time within a few weeks that Trump has declared an energy ceasefire without confirmation from the two warring sides.
Ukraine's European allies on Monday voiced scepticism of any such agreement, spoke strongly in support of Kyiv and [USN:L8N45T1J0 TEXT:"approved the largest set of EU sanctions"] since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.
'WE DO NOT WANT A CEASEFIRE,' KREMLIN SAYS Kyiv has increasingly targeted Russian oil refineries and logistics with long-range strikes in recent months, its answer to more than four-and-a-half years of relentless Russian attacks on its cities, including persistent campaigns to knock out Ukraine's power and heat in successive winters.
Zelenskiy said Ukraine had carried out no attacks on Russian refineries overnight and was willing to agree an energy ceasefire, but only if Russia abided by it. He also said elections, suspended during wartime, could be held in Ukraine if Moscow agreed to a full ceasefire for 60 days.
Russia, for its part, said talks were ongoing about a possible energy ceasefire, and Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said further information would be revealed in due course. But he rejected Zelenskiy's proposal for a full 60-day truce.
"In the Kremlin, both President (Vladimir) Putin and officials at other levels have repeatedly stated that we do not want a ceasefire," said Peskov. "We want long-term peace and are prepared to do everything possible to achieve it."
BODY AMONG WRECKAGE In Kharkiv, Ukraine's second biggest city, rescue workers picked through wreckage of shattered buildings. The body of a dead civilian in jeans and white sneakers lay beneath debris, lit up by floodlights in the nighttime dark.
Nataliia Minka said she had just made it to a shelter when a missile struck nearby. She and her child had seen what they believed to be a missile hitting a nearby power station.
“Ten minutes had passed since they promised they wouldn’t target energy facilities," she said.
“It’s so hard to describe how a child was lying there, already covered up, and the father was running around her, crying and screaming," she added. "It’s so terrifying -- it’s impossible to get through something like this.”
After nighttime attacks killed at least three people in Kharkiv, further strikes took place in the morning, hitting residential buildings and wounding at least 22 more people, municipal officials said. At least three other people were reported killed on Sunday in the western city of Ivano-Frankivsk.
Russia began its latest strike campaign on Ukraine's grid two weeks ago, already causing daily, hours-long power cuts in Kyiv, affecting the capital's water and sewage systems and twice bringing its underground trains to an abrupt halt.
To maintain pressure on Moscow, European Union foreign ministers on Monday added 1,569 new names to their sanctions list of banned individuals and businesses, billed as the largest single package to date.
Germany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Moscow "will only negotiate seriously under pressure, which is why we are sticking to our sanctions against Russia.
"Following Moscow's ruthless attacks on Ukraine's civilian energy infrastructure, we must actually tighten them further."
Trump has increasingly blamed Kyiv's attacks on Russian refineries for surging global costs for fuel, especially diesel, which has hit record prices in the United States since he launched his military campaign against Iran. On Saturday he said Zelenskiy had [USN:L6N45W06G TEXT:""better damn well stop""] attacking Russian refineries.
A person familiar with the situation said the US had threatened to cut off intelligence sharing with Ukraine and supplies of weapons, which Washington no longer provides to Kyiv but allows European countries to buy on its behalf.

items.title: Pope Leo to be hospitalised on Tuesday ahead of lung surgery
items.author: Joshua McElwee
items.creator: Joshua McElwee
items.summary: Pope Leo will go into hospital on Tuesday for surgery to remove a small growth found on one of his lungs, the Vatican said, as the pontiff kept up a busy schedule on Monday, holding seven previously planned meetings in the morning.
items.body:
Pope Leo will go into hospital on Tuesday for surgery to remove a small growth found on one of his lungs, the Vatican said, as the pontiff kept up a busy schedule on Monday, holding seven previously planned meetings in the morning.
Leo, 71, said [USN:L1N45X029 TEXT:"on Sunday"] that the growth, a small nodule, had been found on a recent check-up, was "well-contained" and had been spotted early. Ahead of his hospitalisation, the pope cancelled all his public events from Tuesday until October 20.
The nodule was found during a routine health check, the Vatican press office told journalists earlier on Monday, before confirming that the pope is expected to be hospitalised late on Tuesday morning, ahead of his surgery.
It did not say when the actual operation would take place.
A regular advisory on the pope's daily schedule, issued at noon (1000 GMT) on Monday, said he met that morning with visiting bishops from Argentina, Nicaragua and the United States, among others.
In a meeting at the Vatican with members of a Rome-based charity group on Monday, the pope spoke in a strong, clear voice, thanking them for their work.
COMPLICATION RATE FOR NODULE REMOVAL LOW Leo, elected pope by the world's cardinals in May 2025, is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys sports, including tennis, and is not known to be a smoker or to have had health issues previously.
The Vatican has said the pope's recovery is expected to take about a week.
A nodule on the lung is a small, localised lesion that can be benign. The American Thoracic Society says fewer than 5% of lung nodules overall prove cancerous, although risk rises with age, size, and other factors such as smoking.
Dr. Federico Venuto, chief of thoracic surgery at Rome's Policlinico Umberto I hospital, said surgeries to remove lung nodules are usually minimally invasive, and can sometimes involve use of a thin camera tube called a thoracoscope.
"The complication rate is extremely low," he told Reuters.
POPE'S TRANSPARENCY ABOUT HEALTH UNUSUAL Leo's decision to discuss his upcoming surgery publicly on Sunday marked a contrast with his predecessor, the late Pope Francis, who died in April 2025 at age 88.
Francis was hospitalised several times as he grew frail in his later years and did not usually announce his hospital visits in advance, sometimes sparking a media frenzy over his health.
Canadian Cardinal Gérald Lacroix said on Monday that he was grateful for Leo's transparency.
"I really appreciated yesterday ... (that) he himself said, 'This is what's going on,' very transparent, and asked for prayers," said Lacroix. "I like that."
Leo, the leader of the 1.4-billion-member Church, had several public appointments on his calendar for this week, including a Mass in St. Peter's Square on Wednesday morning.
The Vatican said the Mass would now be led by Filipino Cardinal Luis Tagle, a Vatican official whom Leo [USN:L8N45V0O6 TEXT:"last week"] approved as the dean of the Church's College of Cardinals, in the first selection of an Asian cleric to the elite role.
In the event of a papal death or resignation, the dean of the cardinals is responsible for organizing the secret conclave to elect his successor.
The pope is the final earthly authority for the world's Catholics and does not have a deputy who steps in when he is sick. When a pope is incapacitated, the business of the Vatican's vast bureaucracy carries on as usual, holding off on any decisions that require papal approval.

items.title: パキスタン、カーン元首相派の州首相ら拘束　非常事態宣言
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Asif Shahzad

［イスラマバード　１２日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Asif Shahzad

［イスラマバード　１２日　ロイター］ - パキスタン連邦政府は１２日、北西部カイバル・パクトゥンクワ州のアフリディ州首相らを拘束したと明らかにした。アフリディ氏は収監中のカーン元首相の政党「パキスタン正義運動（ＰＴＩ）」に所属する。ザルダリ大統領は１１日、同州政府がイスラム過激派対策を怠っているとして非常事態を宣言し、州政府の権限を停止した。

チョードリー内務担当国務相はロイターに対し、「州首相と一部の州閣僚が予防拘禁されたことを確認できる」と述べた。拘束は１１日、同州北西部の都市ペシャワルにある州首相公邸で行われたという。訴追すべき案件がある者は起訴して裁判にかけ、それ以外の者は釈放すると述べた。

州首相公邸と周辺の重要施設には多数の警察官と準軍事組織の部隊が配置され、輸送用コンテナで封鎖されている。

同州では１週間前、ＰＴＩ支持者による集会が数日にわたって開かれ、支持者らは、カーン氏の釈放と治療を求めてイスラマバードへ行進する予定だった。

政府とＰＴＩは、９月にデモ行進が呼びかけられて以降、数回にわたって協議を重ねてきた。

チョードリー氏は、政府はデモ行進の容認を含め、ＰＴＩの要求を全て受け入れる用意があったと説明し、「われわれが求めたのはただ一つ、党が武装勢力を公に非難し、武装勢力との戦いでわれわれと手を携えることだった」と述べた。ＰＴＩは同意せず、協議は決裂したという。

items.title: UK proposes rewards for whistleblowers who report economic crimes
items.author: Phoebe Seers
items.creator: Phoebe Seers
items.summary: Britain's Serious Fraud Office is developing plans to reward whistleblowers who report economic crimes such as fraud and bribery, the government said on Monday.
items.body:
Britain's Serious Fraud Office is developing plans to reward whistleblowers who report economic crimes such as fraud and bribery, the government said on Monday.
The move would bring Britain closer to the US model, where financial incentives have been used to encourage people to come forward with evidence of wrongdoing for more than a decade.
Britain has for years debated whether to pay whistleblowers for information. Last year, the tax authority HM Revenue & Customs [USN:L1N3X20S3 TEXT:"introduced the country's first US-style reward scheme"], offering informants up to 30% of tax recovered in major tax cases.
The shift has been driven by the success of overseas programmes, particularly the US Securities and Exchange Commission's whistleblower regime, for which UK nationals are the second-largest overseas user group, the government said.
"We welcome this consultation, having long called for the introduction of a scheme to incentivise whistleblowers. We encourage all those with a view to contribute to the consultation and we look forward to working with our government partners on next steps," a spokesperson for the SFO said.
The change was recommended in a July 2026 review of fraud prosecutions led by lawyer Jonathan Fisher, who said Britain was losing valuable intelligence as whistleblowers chose to report wrongdoing to US authorities that offer financial rewards.
Former SFO Director Nick Ephgrave said in 2024 that paying corporate insiders to provide "smoking gun evidence" could[USN:L5N3EY6O3 TEXT:" significantly increase the speed"] of investigations.
Under proposals set out for public consultation, whistleblowers would be eligible for a reward only if they provide significant, original information that leads to a conviction or enforcement action.
Mirroring the US approach, the government has proposed that rewards be funded from penalties imposed on companies and calculated as a percentage of the amount recovered.
Eliza Lockhart, a senior research fellow at RUSI's Centre for Finance and Security, said rewards recognise whistleblowing as "the provision of an intelligence service" rather than simply an altruistic act.
"If policymakers are serious about tackling economic crime, adopting an intelligence-led approach is crucial," Lockhart said.
Eoin O'Shea, a partner at law firm CMS, said a reward-based system "seems reasonable in principle" given the risks whistleblowers can face, including dismissal or workplace discrimination.
However, critics argue that offering financial rewards could encourage reports motivated by personal gain rather than the public interest.
Jo Mackie, an employment partner at law firm Michelmores, said such incentives created a "moral hazard" and risked undermining internal corporate governance, adding that paying whistleblowers was "fundamentally flawed".

LONDON, Oct 12 : Artificial Intelligence needs urgent global regulation with independent evaluators able to vet new developments, the president of Microsoft said, warning that AI currently faces fewer safety requirements than milk.  
In an interview with the BBC published on Monday, Brad Smith said a set of global safety rules needed to be in place, requiring a "victim" to be informed if their system is breached by a rogue AI agent and an "emergency brake" available.
He said there should also be a legal requirement for companies to write "incident reports". 
"We know how to do this for other products," Smith said. "We should build on that knowledge and think about how to apply it to AI."

"Right now, your washing machine is subject to more safety rules than AI. Every carton of milk that you see in the grocery store is subject to safety rules and inspection."
Tech companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI have started disclosing rogue or undesired behaviour by AI agents as part of a global debate about the fast-advancing technology that has included researchers' warnings of an eventual existential threat to humanity.
Some companies have called for AI development to slow down, but that has sparked a debate as to whether executives have ulterior motives such as setting rules that preserve the lead of their firms, pre-empting a broader government backlash, or simply slowing breakneck spending.
Microsoft's Smith said the one country that was well-placed to lead the way on regulation of AI was Britain, due to the AI Security Institute which was launched under former prime minister, Rishi Sunak. 
Smith said officials in Washington viewed London very differently to how they viewed Brussels, which regulates AI based on the level of risk via its AI Act.
Britain's institute receives pre-deployment access under voluntary agreements with the major AI models, allowing it to assess their capabilities and risks. 
AI Minister Kanishka Narayan has told Reuters that Britain would consider regulating advanced models if the current system proved insufficient.

Dollar hovers near 18-month high as Gulf unrest, US inflation keep investors on edge

NEW YORK/LONDON, Oct 12 : The dollar held near an 18-month high on Monday, supported by safe-haven demand as an escalating Middle East conflict kept investors cautious ahead of key US inflation data later this week.
Oil prices were volatile after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis stepped up strikes on Saudi Arabia, and two tankers were attacked over the weekend. 
Brent crude futures rose 2.09 per cent to $106.80 a barrel, nearing a two-week high, as the attacks overshadowed Sunday's announcement from US President Donald Trump about an energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia. The futures price is still nearly 45 per cent above where it was before the US-Israeli war with Iran started.
The dollar index, which tracks the US currency against six others, was up 0.16 per cent at 102.39, just below last week's 18-month high.

Weekly data from the US markets regulator shows investors have been adding to their bullish positions on the dollar, which rose to around $36 billion in the week to October 7 from $8.4 billion three weeks ago, largely at the expense of the euro.
"Markets got off to a relatively encouraging start to the week, but sentiment has since deteriorated as renewed geopolitical uncertainty and rising oil prices weigh on risk appetite, prompting a fresh round of US dollar demand," said Joel Kruger, a market strategist at LMAX Group in London.
SPOTLIGHT MOVES TO US INFLATION DATA 
Wednesday's US consumer inflation report, one of the last major economic releases before the Federal Reserve's policy meeting this month, could be critical in determining the near-term direction of the dollar. 
Data last week showed US consumer sentiment deteriorated further in early October, as the rising cost of living because of the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy.
The Fed raised rates last month for the first time since 2023 to rein in inflation, with markets keeping a close watch on economic data to gauge whether policymakers may move again. Traders are pricing in an 81 per cent chance of the Fed standing pat this month, up from 51 per cent a month earlier, the CME FedWatch tool showed.
"The real focus is on the CPI number this week, it is likely to be running hot," said Marc Chandler, chief market strategist at Bannockburn Global Forex in New York. He added that a rate hike before an election is so uncommon that "the bar is kind of high" for the Fed to act.
Sharp selloffs in bond markets in the past few weeks worried investors as borrowing costs across the globe rose to multi-decade highs on concern over inflation, energy prices and ballooning government debt. 
The euro fell 0.19 per cent to $1.1180, after clocking a fifth straight week of losses last week, driven by investor angst around France's fiscal health before the 2027 presidential election. The spread between French 10-year yields and safer German yields traded at 140 basis points. Last week it neared 160 bps, the most since 2012.
"It is still too early to tell whether higher borrowing costs will be sufficient to impose greater fiscal discipline on the French government," said OCBC FX strategists. 
Against the yen, the US dollar was a touch higher on the day at 158.57 yen in holiday-thinned trading in Japan, while the pound held steady at $1.323.

Source: Reuters

items.title: L'aéroport de Ryad restera fermé cette semaine après deux attaques meurtrières
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Les autorités saoudiennes ont prolongé lundi pour le reste de la semaine la fermeture de l'aéroport international de Ryad, capitale de l'Arabie saoudite, après que ce dernier a été la cible de deux attaques meurtrières dont une samedi, revendiquée par les Houthis qui a fait 13 morts et plus de 300 blessés.
items.body:
Les autorités saoudiennes ont prolongé lundi pour le reste de la semaine la fermeture de l'aéroport international de Ryad, capitale de l'Arabie saoudite, après que ce dernier a été la cible de deux attaques meurtrières dont une samedi, revendiquée par les [USN:L8N45W036 TEXT:"Houthis"] qui a fait 13 morts et plus de 300 blessés.
Cette attaque a entraîné la décision de fermer l'aéroport dimanche, jour où, selon les termes de la coalition dirigée par l'Arabie saoudite au Yémen, un [USN:L8N45X06H TEXT:""projectile non identifié""] lancé contre le terminal 4 a fait un mort et onze blessés.
L'aéroport international Roi Khaled sera fermé jusqu'au 17 octobre à 21h00 (GMT), selon un message publié par les agences gouvernementales de contrôle de la navigation aérienne.
Les opérations à l'aéroport, le deuxième du pays en termes de fréquentation après celui de Djeddah, ont été suspendues afin de "permettre l'achèvement des procédures visant à garantir la sécurité et la disponibilité opérationnelle des installations de l'aéroport", déclare dans un communiqué l'autorité saoudienne de l'aviation civile.
La compagnie aérienne allemande Lufthansa (LHAG.DE) a annulé tous ses vols à destination de Riyad jusqu'au 16 octobre, tandis qu’Air France-KLM (AIRF.PA) a prolongé jusqu'à la fin du mois la suspension de ses liaisons vers et depuis la capitale saoudienne.
La compagnie Etihad Airways, basée à Abou Dhabi, a également prolongé ses annulations de vols vers l'Arabie saoudite, affectant une vingtaine de vols à destination de Ryad, Djeddah et Dammam lundi et mardi.
Ces attaques perturbent le congrès énergétique du World Petroleum Council qui a commencé dimanche à Ryad, avec notamment la décision de la directrice générale de BP (BP.L) Meg O'Neill d'annuler sa venue.
L'Arabie saoudite a renforcé son engagement militaire au Yémen ces dernières semaines, menant des frappes contre les Houthis et soutenant une contre-offensive des forces gouvernementales après que le groupe s'est emparé le mois dernier de secteurs stratégiques le long de la côte de la mer Rouge.
Les Houthis, les rebelles proches de l'Iran qui contrôlent une bonne partie du Yémen dont la capitale Sanaa, ont dit que toute nouvelle action militaire saoudienne au Yémen entraînerait une riposte de plus grande ampleur, ajoutant que ses actions seraient guidées par le principe de réciprocité.
Les Houthis résistent depuis 2014 à une coalition mise sur pied par l'Arabie saoudite, en s'appuyant sur un arsenal de drones et missiles balistiques constitué avec l'aide de Téhéran.
Les combats font rage depuis des semaines sur plusieurs fronts au Yémen, alors que la guerre civile, globalement latente depuis 2022, a regagné en intensité avec le conflit entre les Etats-Unis et l'Iran.
La coalition menée par l'Arabie saoudite a déclaré avoir détruit un missile balistique lancé par un groupe aligné sur l'Iran en direction de Ryad.
Les autorités saoudiennes avaient auparavant émis une alerte contre une "menace hostile" potentielle dans la capitale, selon un message consulté par Reuters.
Fin septembre, le ministère des Finances saoudien a déclaré que le produit intérieur brut (PIB) du royaume devrait se contracter de 3,6% cette année, en raison notamment des perturbations provoquées sur son activité pétrolière par la guerre entre les Etats-Unis et l'Iran et par le conflit contre les Houthis.

items.title: Europe's STOXX 600 ends higher as bank stocks cushion oil price hit
items.author: Avinash P, Niket Nishant
items.creator: Avinash P, Niket Nishant
items.summary: Europe's equity benchmark rose on Monday, kicking off a busy week on a strong note as a surge in bank shares helped absorb the hit from higher oil prices.
items.body:
Europe's equity benchmark rose on Monday, kicking off a busy week on a strong note as a surge in bank shares helped absorb the hit from higher oil prices.
The pan-European STOXX 600 index (.STOXX) closed 0.65% higher at 635.65 points, posting its second consecutive day of gains.
After weeks of being swayed by broader economic factors such as crude prices and bond yields, investors are expected to zero in on corporate earnings this week.
Strong results could dispel the gloom following renewed tensions in the Middle East. However, France's LVMH (LVMH.PA) reported [USN:L6N45Y0VL TEXT:"worse-than-expected"] third-quarter organic sales growth, as weak demand for its fashion and leather goods weighed.
Its shares closed 1.18% higher ahead of the report, while the luxury sector (.STXLUXP) rose 0.95%.
Semiconductor equipment maker ASML (ASML.AS) and investment firm EQT (EQTAB.ST) are due to report later this week.
BANKS FIND FAVOUR "In areas such as banking, European and Asian stocks could offer stronger value and return potential than their US counterparts," analysts at Julius Baer wrote.
Spain's bank-heavy IBEX (.IBEX) jumped 1.33%, the most among regional peers, while the STOXX 600 banking index (.SX7P) advanced 1.5%.
Oil prices were hovering near two-week highs as attacks on Saudi Arabia overshadowed the prospect of increased supplies after US President Donald Trump hailed fresh Russian diesel exports and a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire covering energy targets.
David Morrison, senior market analyst at Trade Nation, said third-quarter earnings, especially from semiconductor companies and other AI beneficiaries, would be key in shaping near-term market sentiment.
Euro zone bond yields eased on Monday, further helping lift sentiment for riskier assets.
However, yields remain near multi-year highs, reflecting concerns that interest rates will stay higher for longer.
Traders currently expect the European Central Bank to keep rates on hold at its October meeting, while pricing in a quarter-point rate hike in December, according to LSEG-compiled data.
Still, analysts point to limited scope for further ECB tightening given the euro zone's weak growth backdrop.
"The euro area cannot point to robust economic growth. That's simply not the case," Morrison added.
Among other stock moves, Nordex (NDXG.DE) advanced 3.9% after the onshore wind turbine manufacturer said its project order intake in the third quarter rose [USN:L6N45M0JM TEXT:"30% year-on-year"].
Vallourec (VLLP.PA) rose 3.8% after the French steel tube maker won a contract from TotalEnergies (TTEF.PA) for the Absheron gas field in Azerbaijan.
Inwit (INWT.MI) advanced 1.8% after [USN:L1N45Y06D TEXT:"Reuters reported exclusively"] that the telecom towers company's leading shareholders were arranging the financing for a potential take-private deal.
Telecom stocks (.SXKP) were the biggest laggards, down 0.54%.

items.body:
Germany's fragile coalition hit by labour minister's resignation
Reuters | Updated: 12-10-2026 19:48 IST | Created: 12-10-2026 19:48 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Germany's labour minister and co-head of the centre-left Social Democrats (SPD) quit unexpectedly on Monday, adding to uncertainty around Chancellor Friedrich Merz's struggling coalition after bruising state election defeats last month. Baerbel Bas said she was resigning from both positions to deal with grief over her stepdaughter's recent death.
She added that "public attacks against me, unfortunately also from within the ranks of our coalition partner," had made her situation unbearable. Bas will be replaced as minister by Alexander Schweitzer, former state premier of the western state of Rhineland-Palatinate, and the whole of the SPD leadership will face re-election in a special party conference at the end of the year.
While the departure of one minister was not expected to disrupt the overall government, it highlighted the turmoil facing Europe's largest economy. Merz's coalition has been under growing pressure following state election victories for the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) in eastern Germany last month, which it views as the first step towards victory in federal elections due in 2029.
Merz's government is languishing in opinion polls amid economic uncertainty and frustration over living costs. Bas, whose former ministry oversees large parts of Germany's welfare system, was the target of repeated criticism from some members of Merz's conservative Christian Democrats (CDU) who accused her of standing in the way of economic reforms.
Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil, who shared the leadership of the SPD with Bas, cancelled a planned trip to India and it was unclear whether he would attend a meeting of the Group of 20 finance ministers in Thailand this week. STRAINED RELATIONS
Klingbeil said Bas had been subject to "unacceptable" attacks from the CDU while mourning her stepdaughter. But at a press conference, Merz said he had urged his party to show her "every personal consideration, including Christian compassion," in recent weeks.
"I cannot see that we have failed to do so in any way," he said, adding that he was confident new minister Schweitzer would swiftly advance pending legislation and cooperate well within government. Merz was speaking after senior CDU members had held a two-day meeting to seek a way forward after months of coalition wrangling over planned tax, pension and labour laws aimed at reviving Germany's sluggish economy.
"We want to demonstrate our readiness for change – something that is essential given the election results," he added. As part of the leaders' five-page policy paper aimed at addressing voter discontent, he pledged to push ahead with a cut in electricity tax, reviving a measure that was shelved last year because of budget constraints.
While both sides in the coalition agree on the need for reforms to shore up the pension system as the population ages and to help industry confront a surge in energy prices and increasingly intense competition from China, significant differences remain. Merz, a pro-business fiscal conservative, has struggled to win popular support for changes that could push back the retirement age for some, increase the cost of health insurance and weaken worker protections.
Support for the government will be further tested in five more regional elections next year that will impact his ability to get major legislation through the Bundesrat, the upper house of parliament filled by Germany's 16 states.

中国乗用車協会（ＣＰＣＡ）が９日発表したデータによると、上海工場で生産されたセダン「モデル３」とＳＵＶ（スポーツ多目的車）「モデルＹ」の納車台数は、欧州、アジア太平洋地域、カナダへの輸出を含め９万５３６６台と、前年同月の９万０８１２台から増加し、１１カ月連続の前年比プラスとなった。

items.title: アップル供給元の中国立訊精密、米で特許侵害調査　影響軽微と説明
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［上海　１１日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［上海　１１日　ロイター］ - 米アップルに部品を供給する中国の立訊精密工業（ラックスシェア・プレシジョン・インダストリー）は１０日、米国で新たに始まった特許侵害調査による悪影響は軽微との見通しを示した。積極的に対応を進め、株主の利益を守ると説明した。

１０日夜に公表された取引所への届け出に基づく詳細は以下の通り。

＊米国際貿易委員会（ＩＴＣ）は１０月９日、米バイコーによる特許侵害の申し立てを受け、同社と子会社の東莞立訊技術を対象に、米関税法３３７条に基づく調査を開始。

＊ＩＴＣの調査は初期段階。対象は垂直給電システムと関連部品、それらを搭載したコンピューティングシステムで、ＩＴＣはまだ実質的な判断を示していない。

＊対象製品はデータセンター向けの電源モジュールや電力供給ソリューションに使われるもので、まだ量産は開始していない。このため、調査が事業運営や短期的な業績に重大な悪影響を及ぼす可能性は低い。

＊同社は対象の特許と製品の検証を既に開始し、技術、法務、事業の各チームを組織して対応を準備している。

＊顧客やサプライチェーン（供給網）のパートナーとの連携を強化し、会社と株主の利益を積極的に守る。

items.title: 中国の国内自動車販売、12カ月連続減少　輸出は好調維持
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
[北京 １２日 ロイター] - 中国の国内自動車販売は９月、１２カ月連続で減少した。一方、自動車メーカーが国内市場の低迷による影響を和らげようと海外市場に目を向ける中、輸出は引き続き成長を支える主要な要因となった。

中国乗用車協会（ＣＰＣＡ）が１２日発表したデータによると、９月の国内乗用車販売は前年同月比２８．１％減の１６３万台だった。減少率は８月の２３．７％から拡大した。

一方、９月の自動車輸出は前年同月比７３．２％増の９２万３０００台だった。８月は７７．５％増だった。

• 電気自動車（ＥＶ）とプラグインハイブリッド車（ＰＨＶ）の国内販売は前年同月比１６．７％減の１０８万台。８月の１０．１％減から減少率が拡大した。一方、輸出の伸び率は８月の１５４．７％から１６３．５％に加速した。

•

• 電気自動車（ＥＶ）とプラグインハイブリッド車（ＰＨＶ）の国内販売は前年同月比１６．７％減の１０８万台。８月の１０．１％減から減少率が拡大した。一方、輸出の伸び率は８月の１５４．７％から１６３．５％に加速した。

• ＣＰＣＡの崔東樹秘書長（事務局長）は新エネルギー車の輸出ではＥＶが大きな割合を占めるため、ＰＨＶの輸出が制限されても、新エネルギー車全体の輸出に大きな影響が及ぶ可能性は低いと述べた。

• 欧州連合（ＥＵ）のシェフチョビッチ欧州委員（通商担当）は９日、中国とＥＵが、中国からＥＵへのハイブリッド車輸出を４年間で半減させる可能性のある合意に達したと述べた。ただ、輸出数量の上限や、その枠を超える輸出に適用される条件は依然として不明だ。

• 国内販売の減少は、経済全体の弱さを反映している。個人消費の低迷と不動産不況の長期化が需要を圧迫している。

• 規制当局は成長重視から安全性と価値重視へと軸足を移しており、十分な検証を経ない拙速な新車投入を抑える規則を提案している。

Oil falls on hopes Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire will boost supplies

NEW DELHI, Oct 12 : Oil prices slipped on Monday on expectations of more Russian supplies after US President Donald Trump said Ukraine and Russia had agreed to halt attacks on each other's energy facilities following a US diesel-supply deal with Moscow.
Brent crude futures fell 11 cents, or 0.11 per cent, to $104.61 a barrel by 0627 GMT while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at $91.36 a barrel, down 49 cents, or 0.53 per cent. Both benchmarks were down more than 1 per cent earlier in the session.
ICE gasoil futures fell 3 per cent to $1,436 per metric ton after President Trump said on Friday that Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 metric tons (2.25 million barrels) of diesel to US and global markets.
Russia would supply another 500,000 tons in November and a further 1 million tons "immediately thereafter", Trump added. The daily diesel consumption globally is forecast at close to 29 million barrels, according to the International Energy Agency.

Trump also unexpectedly announced on Sunday that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to an energy ceasefire, but Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelenskiy said he was still waiting to see details of the energy ceasefire while Russia did not comment.
The announcements eased some of the immediate supply pressure, Tim Waterer, KCM Trade chief analyst, said.
"Questions remain over the validity and longevity of any such ceasefire, and without clearer evidence that it will actually hold, the extent of the pullback is likely to stay limited," he added.
IEA's Executive Director Fatih Birol said on Sunday that all members should assess whether additional diesel releases are necessary and that countries which have not yet fully delivered pledged volumes accelerate their remaining releases prioritising diesel.
CRUDE SUPPORTED BY MIDDLE EAST CONFLICT
However, the Middle East conflict continued to support Brent crude at above $100 a barrel.
The Houthis claimed responsibility for a Saturday strike on Riyadh's international airport that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300, while Saudi authorities reported that people were injured in a new attack on the airport on Sunday.
US President Donald Trump said on Saturday the United States was considering joining Saudi strikes on the Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the wider war with Iran that the US and Israel launched in February.
In addition, more attacks on tankers sailing through the Strait of Hormuz have been reported so far this month, threatening to dampen a recovery in Middle East crude exports seen in September.
A tanker was struck by a drone in the vicinity of Sohar anchorage, Oman, while another was damaged by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reported over the weekend.
Goldman Sachs raised its Brent crude price forecast for December to $90 a barrel, up from $85 previously, its analysts led by Daan Struyven said in a note.
"We maintain our base case that continued adaptation of Mideast supply will eventually reduce crude oil prices, while potential renewed escalation still poses significant net upside risk," the analysts said, estimating a risk premium of just over $20 a barrel.
"We forecast WTI prices, which are unusually low vs Brent because of high US-Europe shipping costs, to average $81 in December 2026 and $73 in 2027," they added.
In the Gulf of Mexico, energy majors Shell, Chevron and BP were seeking to redeploy personnel and restore production at their platforms after Hurricane Isaias made landfall early on Saturday.

items.title: 印デリーで地下鉄駅閉鎖、選管トップ辞任要求で新たなデモ計画
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [ニューデリー １２日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[ニューデリー １２日 ロイター] - インドのデリーで１２日、野党が有権者名簿の見直しに抗議し最高裁へのデモ行進を計画する中、当局が地下鉄６駅を閉鎖した。

野党各党や若者中心の団体「ゴキブリ人民党（ＣＪＰ）」の支持者らは今月、ほぼ連日街頭に繰り出し、有権者名簿の見直しを巡りギャネシュ・クマール選挙管理委員長の辞任を求めている。抗議活動の参加者らは、見直しがモディ首相の与党インド人民党（ＢＪＰ）に不当に有利に働いているとしている。

２０２５年に始まった見直しでは、死亡者や転居者、所在を確認できなかった人など、日本の人口を上回る１億３０００万人超の名前が有権者名簿から削除された。

選管は特定の政党を優遇しているとの見方を否定し、誤って名簿から削除された有権者は再登録できると説明している。一方、ＢＪＰは、野党が正当な選挙手続きに不当に疑義を呈し、国の民主主義を損なおうとしていると非難している。

警察は週末、ＣＪＰの指導者を含む数千人の抗議参加者を拘束した。ＣＪＰ支持者らがデモ行進を試みたのに対し、数千人の治安部隊がデリー中心部を封鎖して阻止した。

１２日には「治安上の理由」で地下鉄６駅が閉鎖され、警察は２０カ所以上の区間で交通規制や迂回措置を実施した。

最大野党の国民会議派は、最高裁へ行進して長官に覚書を提出し、「票の窃盗」の終結とクマール氏の辞任を要求すると表明。同党を率いるラフル・ガンジー氏は「若者、全ての野党、市民団体、民主主義を信じ、インド憲法を擁護する全ての人が、われわれと共に行進する」とＸに投稿した。

ただ、国民会議派関係者によると、カント最高裁長官はこの問題が既に裁判所で審理中だとして面会要請を断り、司法手続きを通じて対処するよう求めたという。

一方、ＣＪＰは指導部がデリー警察と面会し、平和的な抗議活動を行う日程の提示を「要求する」と表明した。２４時間以内に日程が示されなければ、新たな抗議活動を呼びかけると警告している。

items.title: Malaysia's 1MDB in settlement talks with Deutsche Bank, report says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Malaysia's state fund 1MDB is in talks to settle a legal dispute with Deutsche Bank , local media reported on Monday, as the country continues its efforts to recover billions of dollars in alleged losses from a corruption scandal.
items.body:
Malaysia's state fund 1MDB is in talks to settle a legal dispute with Deutsche Bank (DBKGn.DE) , local media reported on Monday, as the country continues its efforts to recover billions of dollars in alleged losses from a corruption scandal.
US prosecutors have alleged that at least $4.5 billion was stolen from [USN:L6N45A0CE TEXT:"1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB)"], co-founded by former Malaysian Prime Minister Najib Razak, in a complex, globe-spanning scheme by high-level officials and their associates from 2009 to 2014. Malaysia has said billions more remain unaccounted for.
In 2021, 1MDB [USN:L4N2MX1QM TEXT:"sued"] Deutsche and several other financial organisations to recover billions in assets that it said it were linked to misconduct related in the scandal. Deutsche said at the time that it was "not aware of any basis for a legitimate claim against Deutsche Bank."
Lim Chee Wee, a lawyer for 1MDB, told a court in a separate case on Monday that the fund was in talks with Deutsche on a proposed settlement, The Edge financial newspaper reported, without providing details of the dispute.
Lim said he had already passed on details about the talks to the Kuala Lumpur High Court, according to the report.
Malaysia's court website showed that the court was scheduled to hear 1MDB's lawsuit against Deutsche and others on October 26.
Lim declined to comment when contacted by Reuters.
In an emailed statement, Deutsche said: "We continue to feel strongly about our position in the case, which is supported by our particular fact pattern that is differentiated from other defendants, as well as recent developments in ongoing similar cases involving other parties."
"Any potential settlement would need to take this into account," it said.

items.title: 中国、先端技術の監督強化へ　ＡＩ制御・バブル防止で新指針
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［北京　９日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［北京　９日　ロイター］ - 中国は９日、先端技術分野の推進に向けた政策指針を発表した。中国は、米国との対立を背景に、ハイテク製造業や戦略産業への支援を強化しているが、新興分野への盲目的な投資や過剰な拡大に警告を発し、監督体制を強化する方針を示した。人工知能（ＡＩ）を「安全で信頼でき、制御可能」な状態に維持することを目指す。

習近平国家主席は２０２３年に「新質生産力（新たな質の生産力）」という概念を打ち出し、科学研究や技術的な突破口の開拓、中国全土の製造拠点における産業高度化を重視してきた。

新華社によると、中国共産党と国務院（内閣に相当）が発表した指針は「新質生産力の発展は、質の高い発展を推進するための本質的な要請であり、重要な重点事項である」としている。

指針によると、中国はＡＩ理論や中核技術の突破口を目指すとともに、計算能力（コンピューティングパワー）、アルゴリズム、データの供給を強化し、産業用ＡＩ応用の国家実証拠点を設置する。一方でＡＩが「安全で信頼でき、制御可能」であり続けるよう、技術監視、リスク警告、緊急対応の各体制を整備するよう求めた。

「ＡＩプラス」構想を全面的に実施し、ＡＩを活用して従来型産業を高度化させ、コネクテッド新エネルギー車（ＮＥＶ）、ＡＩ搭載のスマートフォンやパソコン、人型ロボットなどのスマート製品の普及を加速させる。

中核技術における「独自かつ破壊的」なイノベーションを強化し、国家主導の「新型挙国体制」を活用して象徴的な製品の開発・展開を加速するとした。

同時に、当局は実体経済を優先し、バブルや産業の空洞化、盲目的な投資、ハイテク分野への「群がるような」殺到を防止すべきと指摘した。

「新質生産力の発展を名目とした違法または不適切な政策の乱用を厳格に禁止する」とし、盲目的な投資によって重大な損失をもたらした担当当局者に責任を負わせると述べた。

また、安全性を確保しつつ、民間用ドローンや空飛ぶタクシー、小型航空機および関連サービスを中心とする「低空経済」の健全で秩序ある発展も求めた。

items.title: Model blitz at Paris motor show as Europe-China rivalry heats up
items.author: Nick Carey, Giulio Piovaccari
items.creator: Nick Carey, Giulio Piovaccari
items.summary: Europe's car industry fought back against rising Chinese competition at the Paris car show on Monday with a wave of new model launches and fresh support from Brussels, even as Chinese automakers expanded their push into the region.
items.body:
Europe's car industry fought back against rising Chinese competition at the Paris car show on Monday with a wave of new model launches and fresh support from Brussels, even as Chinese automakers expanded their push into the region.
The show opened days after the European Union announced a deal with China to curb imports of Chinese hybrid vehicles into the bloc, with a [USN:B5N44302K TEXT:"cap"] of 350,000 a year, according to a European Commission official. While details of the arrangement have yet to be finalised, it was broadly welcomed by European manufacturers, though some said more support would be needed.
Stellantis (STLAM.MI) CEO Antonio Filosa said the deal was a "good milestone", but that the Fiat maker was also seeking help with high energy costs from the Italian government and wanted Brussels to move more quickly on carbon emissions rules.
The flood of Chinese hybrid imports into the EU is "not sustainable", Renault (RENA.PA) CEO Francois Provost said, describing the agreement as "better than a trade war".
Zhao Fei, president of Chinese automaker Changan (000625.SZ) . said he was "not that concerned" by the deal, which he viewed as a precursor to "Made in Europe" local content rules that could be dealt with by setting up production in the region.
Around [USN:L1N45S104 TEXT:"20 Chinese brands"], including BYD (002594.SZ) and Chery (9973.HK) , are attending the show, double their presence in 2024 as they seek growth overseas amid intense competition and weaker demand at home.
Chinese brands have gained share rapidly in Europe over the last three years, while [USN:L4N45Y073 TEXT:"Chinese exports of hybrids"] to the EU's 27-member states tripled to $7.5 billion in the first half of this year, according to Chinese customs.
The EU-China deal could hit BYD, Chery and state-owned SAIC's (600104.SS) MG brand hardest as between them they accounted for 90% of Chinese brand hybrid sales in the EU in the first eight months of 2026, Jefferies analysts said on Sunday.
BYD said the deal amounted to short-term pressure but that it remained committed to Europe.
Underscoring the challenges facing European manufacturers, Volkswagen said on Monday its deliveries fell [USN:L6N45Y0A9 TEXT:"14.3%"] in the third quarter, the steepest quarterly drop in four years, dragged down by a further decline in demand in its top market, China. Deliveries also fell in North America and Western Europe.
As part of its efforts to regain market share in Europe, Stellantis is launching six new models across its European brands at the show and unveiling nine concept cars.
On Sunday evening, CEO Filosa hailed "the reinvention of a European icon" as he unveiled an affordable retro electric version of [USN:L6N3SF0GW TEXT:"Citroen's 2CV"].
The company is also adopting faster Chinese-style development cycles, Chief Technology Officer Ned Curic said, outlining plans to build small EVs in Italy using a platform being developed with China's Leapmotor.
Renault's head of growth, Fabrice Cambolive, [USN:S8N42Q0EZ TEXT:"said"] on Monday the carmaker could increase EV production in France by at least 50% over the next 12 months.
'IF THEY DROP EXPORTS ... THEY DIE' Like other Western motor shows, Paris had been in decline until Chinese automakers began turning up in force four years ago.
Alongside BYD and Chery, this year's show features newer Chinese entrants including Aito, while state-owned Changan is launching its Nevo and Avatr brands in Europe.
Chinese automakers also used the event to outline further European expansion plans. Changan's Zhao [USN:FWN45V1M3 TEXT:"said the company"] was in talks with manufacturers about producing vehicles in Europe and hoped to build its first European-made car in early 2027.
BYD is [USN:L6N45Y0J7 TEXT:"studying the possibility"] of building a factory in France, Executive Vice President Stella Li told broadcaster BFM TV.
The EU imposed tariffs on Chinese-made fully electric vehicles in October 2024. Brussels is also working on "Made in Europe" rules requiring minimum local content levels for EVs to access large parts of the bloc's market.
Agreement between France and Germany on the provisions is "imminent", French President Emmanuel Macron said at the show.
Chinese automakers have sought European production bases ahead of the proposed rules, often in partnership with established manufacturers.
In July, China's [USN:L1N43P0D0 TEXT:"Geely Auto"] (0175.HK) said it would produce electric SUVs at a Ford Motor (F.N) factory in Spain.
Separately, India's Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Stellantis [USN:L4N45Y0L2 TEXT:"said on Monday"] they had expanded their partnership to include technology and product development, with plans to build vehicles in India for more than 50 global markets.
Car sales in China, the world's largest auto market, fell 20% in the first half of 2026, increasing pressure on manufacturers to expand overseas.
As the US market is effectively closed to China's auto industry, Europe has become its top export priority.
"If they drop exports in Europe they die because they can't make the money elsewhere," said Francois Roudier, secretary general of the International Organisation of Motor Vehicle Manufacturers.

items.title: トルコ・パキスタンなど4カ国、フーシ派のサウジ空港攻撃を非難
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [アンカラ １２日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[アンカラ １２日 ロイター] - トルコ、パキスタン、エジプト、サウジアラビアの４カ国は１１日、イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派によるリヤドの国際空港に対する攻撃を非難し、「いかなる口実によっても正当化も容認もできない危険なエスカレーションだ」と表明した。

サウジ当局によると、１１日にリヤドの国際空港に対する新たな攻撃があり、１人が死亡、１１人が負傷した。同空港では前日にも１３人が死亡、３００人以上が負傷する攻撃があり、フーシ派が犯行を認めた。

４カ国は共同声明で、サウジへの連帯と支持を再確認し、攻撃に対抗し、脅威を抑止して再発を防ぐためにサウジが講じる全ての「正当な措置と対応」を全面的に支持すると表明。 

「地域および国際の平和と安全を脅かす今回の攻撃の結果およびそれに伴うあらゆる影響について、フーシ派に全面的な責任があるとみなし、攻撃の即時かつ無条件の停止を要求する」とした。

トルコ、パキスタン、サウジアラビアは８月、「メッカ共同防衛協定」に署名した。加盟国のいずれか１カ国に対する武力攻撃は３カ国全てに対する攻撃と見なすと定めている。３カ国は先週、共同防衛義務を直ちに履行し、サウジに迅速に部隊を展開することで合意した。

トルコのフィダン外相は８日、サウジへの支援方法を検討していると述べたが、部隊派遣や攻撃作戦への参加は否定した。当局筋は７日、トルコが主に防衛・技術面の支援を提供していると述べていた。

items.title: Ｓ＆Ｐ、英格付け「ＡＡ」に据え置き　エネ価格高騰でも経済堅調
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [９日 ロイター] -
items.body:
[９日 ロイター] - 格付け会社Ｓ＆Ｐは９日、英国のソブリン格付けを「ＡＡ／Ａ─１プラス」に据え置き、見通しは「安定的」とした。中東紛争に起因するエネルギー価格高騰にもかかわらず、英経済が底堅さを示していることを理由に挙げた。

第２・四半期の英国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）は前期比０．５％増加し、２０２６年上半期の同国経済は主要７カ国（Ｇ７）の中で最も高い成長率を記録した。

Ｓ＆Ｐは声明で「中東紛争にもかかわらず、個人消費とサービス業、特に宿泊・飲食業や専門サービス業が比較的底堅く推移し、第２・四半期の成長を支えた」と指摘した。

２６年上半期の経済成長が予想を上回ったことを踏まえ、Ｓ＆Ｐは２６年の英成長率見通しを１．３％に引き上げ、２７─２９年は平均１．４％の成長を見込むとした。

バーナム首相率いる新政権は、財政圧力の高まりと借り入れコストの上昇に直面する中、経済政策の見直しを目指している。

Ｓ＆Ｐは、議会で過半数議席を握っていることがバーナム氏に政策課題を推進する裁量を与えているものの、生計費高騰という大きなショックへの対応が必要となっており、歳出計画は歳入の制約や、過度に高い税負担による成長鈍化リスクとのバランスを取る必要があるとした。

Pakistan sees growth above 4%, looks to raise more than US$1 billion from privatisation

Pakistan Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb poses after a Reuters interview in the IMF/World Bank 2026 Annual Meetings at the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center (QSNCC) in Bangkok, Thailand, on Oct 12, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Patipat Janthong)

FAST

BANGKOK: Pakistan's economy is expected to grow by more than 4 per cent this fiscal year despite elevated oil prices, as the government looks to push for the privatisation of five to six entities that could raise upwards of US$1 billion, Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb told Reuters on Monday (Oct 12).
Pakistan's economy is considered to be highly vulnerable to a prolonged Middle East conflict given its dependence on Gulf energy imports, remittances and financing support from the region, even as it remains reliant on external financing to bolster foreign exchange reserves and meet debt repayments.
The South Asian country of 255 million people has been able to procure adequate quantities of fuel, successfully avoiding any shortages, and critical sectors such as agriculture were holding up, Aurangzeb said.
"So I'm still quite clear that we should clock north of 4 per cent," he said in an interview on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank in Bangkok.

"And on the inflation side, obviously, we are keeping a very close eye because it does have a knock-on impact in terms of the commodity prices."
Following a period of severe economic turmoil exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, the cash-strapped economy has recovered some of its footing, supported by a US$7 billion, 37-month IMF loan program known as the Extended Fund Facility signed in 2024 that includes some tough measures such as raising tax revenue on farm income.
EXCHANGE STABILISATION FACILITY  The US-Israeli-led war with Iran, now in its eighth month, and the inflation and hardship it has caused, will dominate the agenda and sideline conversations during the meetings that are being held outside Washington for the first time in three years.
Pakistan, which reached a staff-level agreement with the IMF last week potentially unlocking about US$1.21 billion in financing under the Extended Fund Facility and a climate program, is continuing discussions with the United States for a proposed US$10 billion exchange stabilisation facility, Aurangzeb said.
But he declined to provide a time frame for the conclusion of negotiations.
"If it comes through, this will be a great help for us," he said, referring to the facility, which is in addition to ongoing talks with the Export-Import Bank of the United States (EXIM) and the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC).
"If it doesn't come through, this does not, you know, create any problem for us in terms of access to market."
PRIVATISATION PUSH Following the privatisation of flag carrier Pakistan International Airlines last year, Aurangzeb said the government has around another dozen entities in the pipeline, including state-owned power distribution companies and the outsourcing of airport operations.
"I expect about five or six of these to go through during this fiscal year," he said, adding that they could raise more than US$1 billion.
Privatisation has been seen as a key test of Pakistan's reform credibility with the IMF, with officials previously underlining that failure to offload loss-making state firms risked renewed pressure on public finances.
"We are quite clear that we want the private sector to lead the country," said Aurangzeb. "So our role is to help support, assist any way we can in terms of the ecosystem."

items.title: ＡＩ投資で世界成長率約3％維持、アジアに大きな恩恵＝ＩＭＦ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Andrea Shalal

[バンコク １２日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Andrea Shalal

[バンコク １２日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）のゲオルギエワ専務理事は１２日、人工知能（ＡＩ）インフラへの旺盛な投資によって世界経済の成長率が３％前後に維持されており、タイなどハードウエアを供給する多くのアジア諸国が大きな恩恵を受けているという認識を示した。

タイの首都バンコクでこの日開幕したＩＭＦ・世界銀行年次総会で、ＡＩ投資ブームは既に「需要ショック、投資ショック」をもたらしていると指摘。アジア先進国の経済成長率を０．５─１．０％ポイント、アジア新興国の成長率を０．２─０．８％ポイント押し上げる可能性があると述べた。

「エネルギー供給ショックが足かせとなっているにもかかわらず、世界経済が３％前後の成長を維持しているのは、こうした投資の加速によるものだ」と語った。

ＩＭＦは７月、２０２６年の世界経済成長率を３％と予測した。１３日に最新の見通しを公表する。

＜ＡＩがもたらす大きな影響＞

ゲオルギエワ氏は、ＡＩを「ゆっくりと押し寄せる津波」に例え、雇用や成長、教育に大きな影響を及ぼすと指摘。労働から資本への移行が見込まれることから、政府が課税を通じて税収を確保する仕組みにも大きな影響が及ぶとの見方を示した。 

ＩＭＦの推計では、ＡＩによって、時間の経過とともに雇用の４０％が能力強化、あるいは質や価値の低下、消失につながる可能性があるという。初期の調査では、米国の雇用の１０％で既にＡＩスキルが求められていることが示された。定型的な反復作業を伴う仕事が減る一方、賃金水準が比較的低い建設とデータセンターの２分野では、低賃金の仕事が増えているという。   

ゲオルギエワ氏は「ＡＩは変革をもたらす技術だ。われわれの働き方や暮らし方を根本から変える」と述べ、自身も今ではＡＩアシスタントから毎日、予定について３０秒間の案内を受けていると紹介した。

ＡＩのサプライチェーン（供給網）では米国、中国、インドが最も重要な生産国だが、必要なインフラを構築する企業の多くはアジアにあると指摘。今年の年次総会の開催国タイにも言及した。

＜新卒採用への影響＞

雇用問題を総裁任期中の中心課題に掲げる世界銀行のバンガ総裁は、世銀が大規模言語モデルに依存しない「スモールＡＩ」の活用に重点を置き、新興国市場の農家、医療制度、教育関係者などに大きな生産性向上をもたらすことを目指していると述べた。 

同じイベントに登壇したシンガポールのシャンムガラトナム大統領は、ＡＩによって新卒者の就職機会が減っている問題に各国政府が対応すべきだと述べた。

「われわれが早急に取り組まなければならない問題がある。就業の最初の段階、つまり卒業後に初めて就く仕事への需要が今減っていることだ」と語った。

ＡＩが途上国と先進国の間で、成長と雇用創出を巡る「新たな格差」を生むことにも警戒すべきだと指摘した。
